questions.ref: p. 44, Other Markings: a double solid white line prohibits lane changing.

questions.q: A 19-year-old with no previous license applies for a Connecticut learner's permit. What is the minimum time the permit must be held before the road test?
options: 120 days
180 days
30 days
90 days
questions.ref: p. 7, Applicants 18 Years of Age or Older: must hold a learner's permit for at least 90 days before the road test.

questions.q: Which statement about the vehicle used for a Connecticut road test is correct?
options: A rented vehicle may be used by an applicant with no valid license if the rental company provides proof of insurance
A long-term leased vehicle may be used if its insurance identifies the vehicle and the lease company
An unlicensed applicant may drive alone to the test location if it is nearby
A vehicle with no valid registration may be used if it is insured
questions.ref: p. 7, The Road Test: vehicle must have valid registration and proof of insurance; long-term leased vehicles properly insured may be used; no rentals without a valid license; unlicensed operator cannot drive to the test alone.

questions.q: How many hours of instruction must a parent or legal guardian complete with a teen who obtains a learner's permit?
options: Four hours, covering the effects of alcohol and drugs on drivers and the penalties for violations
Eight hours, covering all material in the driver's manual
Two hours, on the laws governing drivers under 18 and the dangers of teen driving
Thirty hours, covering classroom instruction
questions.ref: p. 6, Parent Training Requirements: two hours of instruction concerning the laws governing drivers under 18 and the dangers of teen driving.

questions.q: A 17-year-old is convicted for the second time of using a hands-free phone while driving. What is the penalty?
options: A 90-day suspension and a $175 license restoration fee
A 30-day suspension and a $175 license restoration fee
A 60-day suspension and a $175 license restoration fee
A 6-month suspension and a $175 license restoration fee
questions.ref: p. 34, suspension table: cell phone use brings 30 days (1st), 90 days (2nd), and 6 months (3rd). Drivers 16/17 may not use even hands-free devices (p. 8).

questions.q: You want to check your tire pressure with a gauge. Where does the manual say you can find the recommended psi?
options: On the tire sidewall, which always lists the exact pressure that you should inflate the tire to
On the dashboard panel next to the warning light that shows the tire pressure symbol
On the registration card that you are required to keep in the vehicle at all times
In the vehicle owner's manual or on the driver's side door jamb of the vehicle
questions.ref: p. 11, Tires: the recommended psi is located in the vehicle owner's manual or the driver's side door jamb; use a tire pressure gauge to check it.

questions.q: A vehicle bounces a lot after a bump or a stop and is hard to control. According to the manual, which parts may need to be replaced?
options: Worn brake pads and rotors in the braking system
A leaking muffler or exhaust pipe in the exhaust system
New shocks or other suspension parts
Cracked wiper blades or a damaged washer bottle
questions.ref: p. 12, Suspension System: if the vehicle bounces a lot after a bump or a stop, or is hard to control, you may need new shocks or other suspension parts; have a mechanic check it.

questions.q: An adult driver is wearing a seat belt, but an adult passenger in the back seat is not. What may happen?
options: Both the driver and the passenger could be cited and fined $75
Only the passenger can be cited
Only the driver can be cited
Neither can be cited, because back-seat adults are exempt
questions.ref: pp. 12-13, Seat Belt Laws: if either the driver or passenger fails to wear the belt, each could be cited and fined $75.

questions.q: When you finish a sharp turn using the hand-over-hand technique, how should you straighten the steering wheel?
options: Let the wheel slip back through your fingers to save time
Straighten it by hand rather than letting it slip through your fingers
Release the wheel so it straightens itself
Pull it back with one hand while shifting
questions.ref: p. 14, Steering, Hand-over-Hand: when you complete a turn, straighten out the wheel by hand; letting it slip through your fingers could be dangerous.

questions.q: You are driving on a road with exit ramps and want to exit. When should you begin to slow down?
options: As soon as you signal, while still in the main lane
A quarter mile before the exit
As soon as you can see the exit sign
Not until you have moved onto the exit ramp
questions.ref: p. 21, Space to Leave: keep up with the speed of traffic on the main road; do not slow down until you move onto the exit ramp.

questions.q: You are on a two-lane road with no right lane and a driver is following you very closely. What should you do?
options: Wait until the road ahead is clear, then reduce your speed slowly
Brake hard for a moment to make the tailgater back off
Speed up to stay ahead of the tailgater
Stop on the road and let the tailgater pass
questions.ref: p. 22, Being Tailgated: if no right lane, wait until the road ahead is clear and reduce speed slowly; never slow down quickly to discourage a tailgater.

questions.q: You are driving on a road with two lanes in your direction and you are not passing or turning left. Which lane should you use?
options: The left lane, since it is for faster traffic
Either lane, as long as you signal your lane changes and do not exceed the posted speed limit at any time
The right lane, since Connecticut law requires it with fewer than three lanes in your direction
The left lane if you are traveling faster than the cars to your right
questions.ref: p. 23, On Multi-Lane roads: when direction of travel is less than three lanes, Connecticut law requires you to drive in the right lane except when passing.

questions.q: A bicyclist is riding slowly in the travel lane on a two-lane road marked with a double solid yellow line. When may you pass?
options: Never, because crossing a double solid yellow line to pass any vehicle, including a bicycle, is always illegal
Only if you can see far enough ahead to pass safely and leave at least three feet of space
Only after sounding your horn to warn the bicyclist
Only if the bicyclist moves onto the shoulder
questions.ref: pp. 17-18: you may pass slow moving vehicles, including bicyclists, in a no passing zone if you can do so safely (cross the double yellow only if you can see far enough ahead), with a minimum of three feet.

questions.q: Why should you resist the temptation to pass on the right of a truck that is approaching an intersection?
options: Trucks always have the right-of-way at intersections
The rear wheels of a truck follow a longer path than its front wheels
Trucks cannot make right turns without stopping first
If the truck turns right, you could be caught between the truck and the curb
questions.ref: p. 20, Trucks Make Wide Right Turns: resist passing on the right of a truck approaching an intersection; if the driver turns right you could be caught between the truck and the curb. (Rear wheels follow a shorter path.)

questions.q: A school bus ahead has stopped with its red lights flashing, and they have just stopped flashing. What should you do?
options: Watch for children along the road and wait until they have left the roadway and it is safe
Proceed immediately, since the bus lights have stopped flashing and the children are already on board
Proceed as soon as the bus starts to move
Proceed slowly while sounding your horn
questions.ref: p. 37, Right-of-Way: after the school bus lights stop flashing, watch for children and do not proceed until they have completely left the roadway and it is safe.

questions.q: You see an orange triangle on the back of a vehicle. What does it mean?
options: The vehicle is disabled and stopped on the road
The vehicle is carrying hazardous materials and is required to stop at all railroad crossings
A slow-moving vehicle, such as a farm tractor, usually traveling 25 mph or less
The vehicle is an emergency vehicle responding to a call
questions.ref: p. 18, Slow Moving Vehicles: farm tractors, animal-drawn and roadway maintenance vehicles usually go 25 mph or less and display an orange triangle slow-moving decal.

questions.q: You are following a motorcyclist on a road with potholes and loose gravel. What does the manual say to expect?
options: The rider will hold a steady line, because motorcycles handle gravel and potholes just as safely as cars do
The rider will stop completely and wait for you to pass, so you should move up close behind to be ready
The rider will move onto the shoulder, so you should speed up to keep pace in the vacated lane
The rider may suddenly change lanes or speed to avoid the hazard, so you should allow room for the motorcyclist to maneuver
questions.ref: p. 18, Motorcycles: obstacles minor to a motorist, such as potholes and gravel, can be deadly to a motorcyclist; be prepared for sudden changes in lanes or speed and allow room to maneuver.

questions.q: Why can the pavement on a bridge be icy even when other pavement is not?
options: Bridges are always shaded by trees and tall buildings along the water
Bridges have no earth underneath to insulate them
Bridges are never treated with road salt
Water from rivers freezes on the pavement
questions.ref: p. 25, Slippery Roads: bridges do not have earth underneath to insulate them, so they can be colder and icier than other roadways.

questions.q: According to the manual, people with untreated obstructive sleep apnea are how many times more likely to fall asleep at the wheel?
options: 7 times
2 times
6 times
10 times
questions.ref: p. 28, Fatigue: untreated obstructive sleep apnea makes drivers 7 times more likely to fall asleep at the wheel (night shift work increases the risk by nearly 6 times).

questions.q: After drinking several beers at a party, you want to drive home in an hour. What will sober you up?
options: Drinking several cups of strong coffee
Taking a cold shower
Only the passage of time
Walking outside in the fresh air
questions.ref: p. 33, Alcohol and You: there is no way to sober up quickly; coffee, fresh air, exercise, or cold showers will not help; time is the only thing.

questions.q: A driver completes the DMV operator retraining program and commits another moving violation 18 months later. What results?
options: No suspension, because more than one year has passed
A license suspension of at least 30 days
A suspension of at least 45 days
A suspension of at least 90 days
questions.ref: p. 35, Operator Retraining Program: an additional moving violation within three years of completion results in a suspension of at least 30 days.

questions.q: You are driving in a roundabout and a driver on another approach is waiting to enter. What should you do?
options: Keep moving; do not stop within the roundabout to allow that driver to enter
Stop and wave the driver into the roundabout
Stop, because entering traffic has the right-of-way
Slow to a crawl until the driver enters
questions.ref: p. 37, Roundabouts: entering traffic must yield to circulating traffic; do not stop within the roundabout to allow traffic to enter from another leg.

questions.q: Your gas pedal sticks and the motor keeps going faster and faster. What should you do?
options: Turn the ignition to the lock position right away to shut off the engine and stop the acceleration
Shift into park while still moving
Pump the brake pedal until the engine slows
Keep your eyes on the road, shift to neutral, pull off when safe, and turn off the engine
questions.ref: p. 40, Gas Pedal Sticks: keep eyes on the road, shift to neutral, pull off when safe, turn off engine. Never turn the ignition to 'lock' while moving.

questions.q: You are already in the intersection when the traffic light turns yellow. What should you do?
options: Stop immediately
Do not stop; continue through the intersection
Back up behind the stop line
Stop only if there is no traffic behind you
questions.ref: p. 45, Traffic Signals: if you are in the intersection when the yellow light comes on, do not stop; continue through.

questions.q: You are about to cross railroad tracks in a car with a manual transmission. What does the manual advise?
options: Shift to a lower gear while on the tracks so that you have extra power if a train appears
Shift into neutral and coast over the tracks so that the engine cannot stall on the crossing
Do not shift gears while crossing the tracks, because you might stall the vehicle
Downshift just before the tracks and accelerate hard so you spend the least time on them
questions.ref: p. 51, Railroad Crossing Signs: it is wise not to shift gears when crossing railroad tracks because you might stall.

questions.q: A yellow warning sign tells you that a divided highway begins ahead. What does this mean?
options: The divided roadway ends ahead and two-way traffic resumes, so you should watch for oncoming vehicles
The number of traffic lanes in your direction is being reduced, so you should be ready to merge
A sharp curve or a narrow bridge is ahead, so you should slow down and follow the arrows
The highway ahead splits into two separate one-way roadways divided by a median, so you should keep right
questions.ref: p. 50, Divided Highway Begins: the highway ahead is split into two separate roadways by a median or divider and each roadway is one-way; keep right.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT prohibited for a 16- or 17-year-old licensed driver?
options: Driving to work at 11:30 p.m. for a job
Using a hands-free device while driving
Carrying more passengers than there are seat belts
Operating a vanpool vehicle
questions.ref: p. 8: employment travel is an exception to the 11 p.m.-5 a.m. curfew; hands-free devices, excess passengers, and vanpool vehicles are all prohibited.

questions.q: When a learner's permit holder is driving, where must the person giving instruction sit?
options: In the rear seat, so the learner is not distracted
In any seat, if the instructor holds a valid license
In the front passenger seat next to the learner, alert and ready to take over
In the front passenger seat, though the instructor may rest while the learner drives
questions.ref: p. 5, Qualified Trainer Requirement: the instructor must sit in the front passenger seat and be alert and ready to take over.

questions.q: A 17-year-old completes 30 hours of classroom training and at least 8 hours of behind-the-wheel training at a Connecticut commercial driving school, and the rest of the 40 hours at home. How soon after the permit is issued may the teen begin testing?
options: 90 days
120 days
180 days
60 days
questions.ref: p. 6, Home Training Program: applicants with the full 30 hours classroom and at least 8 hours behind-the-wheel from a CT commercial driving school are eligible in 120 days; all others wait 180 days.

questions.q: Which offense cannot be considered for youthful offender status for someone under age 18?
options: Reckless driving
Street racing
Operating while under suspension
Driving under the influence of alcohol or drugs
questions.ref: p. 35, Youthful Offender Status: negligent homicide, evading responsibility after a death/serious injury, and DUI cannot be considered; reckless driving, street racing and operating under suspension are on the other list.

questions.q: Which of the following is legal for a 30-year-old driver in Connecticut?
options: Holding a phone to talk while stopped at a traffic light
Using a hands-free mobile phone accessory while driving
Texting while stopped in traffic
Using a laptop computer while stopped at a stop sign
questions.ref: p. 13, Cell Phone Laws: drivers are permitted only to use hands-free accessories; hand-held use is prohibited even when temporarily stopped.

questions.q: A parent wants to place a rear-facing infant seat in the front passenger seat of a vehicle with a functional passenger-side airbag. Under Connecticut law, this is:
options: Prohibited
Permitted if the infant weighs less than 30 pounds
Permitted if the seat has a five-point harness
Permitted if the seat is also secured with the vehicle's seat belt
questions.ref: p. 12, Child Safety Requirements: the law prohibits placing a rear-facing child restraint in the front seat of a vehicle with a functional passenger side airbag.

questions.q: After a heavy snowfall, what must you do before driving?
options: Clear only a small area of the windshield in front of the driver
Clear the windshield and defrost it; the side windows can wait
Clear the windshield and driver's side window only
Clear snow, ice, or frost from all windows
questions.ref: p. 11, Windshield, Wipers, Windows: clear snow, ice, or frost from all windows before driving.

questions.q: You see a sign that warns of a lane closure ahead in a work zone. When should you merge into the open lane?
options: At the very end of the closing lane
Only after passing the first flagger
As soon as possible, at first notice of the approaching work zone
After speeding up to pass vehicles in the open lane
questions.ref: p. 16, Work zone safety tips: merge as soon as possible; move to the appropriate lane at first notice of an approaching work zone.

questions.q: You have been stopped at a red light and it turns green. Cross traffic has a red light. What does the manual advise?
options: Proceed at once, because traffic facing the red light is required to stop and the green light gives you the right-of-way over everyone
Look only to the left, since that is where the nearest crossing traffic will come from, and then proceed with the flow of traffic
Sound your horn once to warn red-light drivers who may still be entering, and then accelerate through the intersection
Allow crossing traffic to clear, and still look left and right, because cross-street drivers are most likely to hurry through just after the light turns green
questions.ref: p. 15, Intersections: look left and right even if other traffic has a red light, especially just after the light turns green; if you are stopped and the light turns green, allow crossing traffic to clear (p. 45).

questions.q: Which statement about passing is correct?
options: You may pass on a paved shoulder if the vehicle ahead is turning left
You may pass at a shopping center entrance if no vehicle is visible
You should pass several vehicles at once to spend less time in the oncoming lane
Never pass on the shoulder, whether it is paved or not
questions.ref: p. 23: never pass on the shoulder; do not pass where a vehicle is likely to enter or cross the road (intersections, railroad crossings, shopping center entrances); pass one vehicle at a time.

questions.q: You are on an entrance ramp and see no space to merge into heavy highway traffic. What should you do?
options: Drive to the end of the ramp and stop
Slow down on the ramp so you have room to speed up before merging
Stop on the ramp and wait for traffic to clear
Merge anyway and expect other drivers to make room for you by slowing down
questions.ref: p. 20, Space to Enter: do not drive to the end of the ramp and stop; if you must wait for space, slow down on the ramp so you have room to speed up.

questions.q: You are about to pass a bicyclist on a narrow road and an oncoming vehicle is approaching. What should you do?
options: Speed up to pass the bicyclist before the oncoming vehicle arrives
Pass the bicyclist at once, staying as close as possible to the centerline so you stay clear of the bicyclist's lane position
Slow down, let the oncoming vehicle pass first, then give the bicyclist at least three feet
Sound your horn so the bicyclist moves off the road
questions.ref: p. 22, Space to the Side: take hazards one at a time; slow down and let the vehicle pass first so you can give the bicycle at least three feet.

questions.q: You are approaching an intersection with a bike lane and plan to turn right. What should you do?
options: Move into the bike lane early to prepare for the turn, since bike lanes may be used on approaches to turns
Honk to warn bicyclists, then turn
Never cross a bike lane, even to turn
Yield to bicyclists and turn across the lane without driving in the bike lane beforehand
questions.ref: p. 17: you must yield to bicyclists in a bicycle lane before you turn across it; you may turn across a bike lane but may not drive in it when approaching a turn.

questions.q: You are parked on the street and about to open your driver's door. What should you do first?
options: Check to the sides and rear for bicyclists and other traffic
Open the door slightly and wait for traffic to react
Tap your horn to alert approaching bicyclists
Look only straight ahead, since traffic cannot approach from behind
questions.ref: pp. 16-17: when parked on the street, check to the sides and rear for bicyclists before opening the door; do not open a door that gets in the way of moving traffic.

questions.q: How far can the blind spots of a truck extend in front of the cab and behind the truck?
options: Up to about 200 feet in front of the cab and about 20 feet behind the truck
Up to about 20 feet in front of the cab and about 200 feet behind the truck
Up to about 65 feet in front of the cab and about 20 feet behind the truck
Up to about 5 feet in front of the cab and about 50 feet behind the truck
questions.ref: p. 19, Wide Turns: blind spots may stretch up to 20 feet in front of the cab and approximately 200 feet behind the truck.

questions.q: A bus traveling in the lane next to you signals and begins moving into your lane. What are you required to do?
options: Speed up to stay ahead of the bus
Maintain your speed, since you hold the lane
Yield the right-of-way to the bus
Tap your horn and hold your position
questions.ref: p. 18 and p. 37: drivers are required to yield the right-of-way to a bus traveling in the same direction when the bus appropriately signals.

questions.q: What is the best way to handle a sharp curve?
options: Slow down before you enter the curve so you do not have to brake in it
Brake firmly while in the curve to keep control
Accelerate through the curve to maintain traction
Enter at the speed limit and brake lightly in the middle
questions.ref: p. 25, Curves: always slow down before you enter the curve so you do not have to brake in the curve; braking in a curve can cause a skid.

questions.q: You notice a driver ahead drifting over the lane lines while looking at a map. What should you do?
options: Follow closely and flash your lights to get the driver's attention before the driver drifts further
Pass quickly on the right
Flash your headlights and sound your horn repeatedly
Give the driver plenty of room and keep 3 to 4 seconds of following distance
questions.ref: p. 27, Driver Distractions: give a distracted driver plenty of room and maintain a following distance of 3 to 4 seconds; be careful passing.

questions.q: Connecticut's zero tolerance law for drivers under age 21 applies where?
options: Only on public roads
On both public roads and private property
Only on highways and expressways
Only when the driver is also driving erratically
questions.ref: p. 33, Alcohol and the Law: under-21 drivers face penalties for any measurable alcohol (.02% or more) on both public roads and private property.

questions.q: Before driving after taking an over-the-counter allergy medication, what should you do?
options: Nothing, since over-the-counter medicines are sold freely and do not affect driving ability
Drink a cup of coffee to offset any drowsiness
Check the label for warnings and ask a doctor or pharmacist if unsure
Wait about 30 minutes and then drive
questions.ref: p. 33, Drugs and Driving: drugs for allergies can make a person drowsy; check the label and ask your doctor or pharmacist if unsure.

questions.q: You are making a legal U-turn. Which lane should you move into?
options: The outside or right-hand lane traveling in the opposite direction
The inside or left lane traveling in the opposite direction
Whichever lane is open, as long as you signal
The center turn lane
questions.ref: p. 37, U-Turns: give a left turn signal, stop, check for approaching traffic, and proceed into the outside or right-hand lane traveling in the opposite direction.

questions.q: Your car has an Antilock Braking System (ABS) and you must stop quickly. What should you do?
options: Press on the brake pedal as hard as you can and keep pressing, even if you feel the pedal pushing back
Pump the brake pedal repeatedly so that the wheels never lock, and ease off if you feel the pedal pushing back
Press the pedal hard, then release it as soon as it pushes back, and press again once the car stops skidding
Apply the brakes lightly at first and steer away from the hazard, adding pressure only if the car begins to skid
questions.ref: p. 40, Avoiding Collisions, Stopping Quickly: with ABS, press the brake pedal as hard as you can and keep pressing; you might feel the pedal pushing back, and ABS only works with the pedal pushed down.

questions.q: On a divided highway, a solid yellow line runs along the left side of your roadway. What does it indicate?
options: The center of a roadway with opposing traffic
A reversible lane
The left edge of the roadway
The right edge of the roadway
questions.ref: p. 43, Edge Lines: solid white lines are used on the right of the roadway edge; solid yellow lines are used on the left edge of divided roadways.

questions.q: You are turning left on a green arrow when it changes to a yellow arrow. What does it mean?
options: Oncoming traffic is stopped, so you may turn freely
The protection of the green arrow is ending, and you should prepare to stop
You must stop immediately in the middle of the intersection
You may turn only if no pedestrians are in the crosswalk
questions.ref: p. 45, Arrows: a yellow arrow means the protection of a green arrow is ending; if turning in the direction of the arrow, prepare to stop.

questions.q: At a railroad crossing with flashing lights and a gate, a train has just passed. When may you proceed?
options: As soon as the train has passed, by driving around the lowered gate
After looking both ways, even if the gate is still lowered
As soon as the train has passed, even if the lights are still flashing
Only after the gates are raised and the lights stop flashing
questions.ref: p. 52, Railroad Crossbuck, Flashing Lights and Gate: remain stopped until the gates are raised and the lights stop flashing; do not drive around the lowered gate.

questions.q: A 17-year-old completes driver education through a licensed commercial driving school. How long after the learner's permit was issued must the teen wait before taking the road test?
options: 90 days
120 days
180 days
60 days
questions.ref: p.6 Commercial Driving School Training: applicants who complete driver education at a commercial or secondary school wait 120 days after permit issuance; all others wait 180 days.

questions.q: Maya is 16 and has held her Connecticut driver's license for eight months. Which passenger may she carry in addition to those allowed during her first six months?
options: A 17-year-old friend, as long as there are enough seat belts
A 19-year-old neighbor who has held a license for three years
Any two classmates, provided one of them holds a license
Her younger brother, a member of her immediate family
questions.ref: p.8 Passenger Restrictions: during months seven through twelve the only additional passengers allowed are members of the driver's immediate family.

questions.q: Which statement about a Connecticut learner's permit is correct?
options: It is valid until you obtain a driver's license or 2 years from the date it is issued, whichever comes first.
It is valid for 1 year from the date of issue and must then be renewed at a DMV office with another knowledge test.
It must be carried only when you are driving on highways.
It can be issued at age 15 if a parent completes the two-hour parent training.
questions.ref: p.4-5 Learner's permit: must be at least 16; permit valid until license obtained or 2 years from issue; permit holder must carry the permit whenever operating a vehicle.

questions.q: A licensed 17-year-old is convicted a second time of using a cell phone while driving. What suspension does DMV impose?
options: 30-day suspension
6-month suspension
90-day suspension
1-year suspension
questions.ref: p.34 suspension table: cell phone/text messaging is 30 days (1st), 90 days (2nd), 6 months (3rd).

questions.q: A child is 18 months old and weighs 34 pounds. Which restraint is required under Connecticut's child restraint rules?
options: A rear-facing car seat with a 5-point harness
A forward-facing seat with a 5-point harness
A booster seat used with the vehicle lap and shoulder belt
Any 5-point harness seat, since the child weighs more than 30 pounds
questions.ref: p.12 Child Safety Requirements: under age 2 requires rear-facing; if age and weight fall in two categories the more restrictive requirement (rear-facing) applies.

questions.q: A driver says he skips his seat belt when 'just driving around town.' Which fact from the manual contradicts that thinking?
options: Most traffic deaths happen on highways posted at 55 mph or more, not on local roads
Most traffic deaths happen more than 50 miles from home on long trips on unfamiliar roads
Over half of all traffic deaths happen within 25 miles of home
The seat belt law applies only on roads posted above 45 mph or on trips beyond 25 miles
questions.ref: p.13 Misconceptions: over half of all traffic deaths happen within 25 miles of home, many on roads posted at less than 45 mph.

questions.q: A registered vehicle's insurance lapses and the insurance company reports the cancellation to DMV. If the owner fails to respond to DMV's warning notice, what happens?
options: The owner's driver's license is suspended for 45 days
The registration is suspended
The vehicle is impounded until proof of insurance is shown
The owner automatically enters an Insurance Compliance agreement
questions.ref: p.13 Insurance Laws: failure to respond to your warning notice will result in suspension of the registration.

questions.q: Safer drivers look at least 12 seconds ahead of their vehicles. On the highway, about how far is 12 seconds?
options: About one city block
About one-third of a mile
About half a mile
About four city blocks (a quarter mile)
questions.ref: p.14 Look Ahead: in the city 12 seconds is about one block; on the highway it is about four city blocks (a quarter of a mile).

questions.q: You are on an entrance ramp to a high-speed road and traffic in the main lane is too heavy to merge right away. What should you do?
options: Slow down on the ramp so you still have room to speed up before merging
Drive to the end of the ramp and stop to wait for a gap
Pull onto the shoulder of the main road and wait for a gap
Keep full speed and force your way in, since traffic should make room
questions.ref: p.20 Space to Enter: if you must wait for space, slow down on the ramp so you have room to speed up; do not drive to the end of the ramp and stop.

questions.q: You are traveling at 55 mph on a two-lane road and want to pass. About how much clear distance do you need, counting the oncoming vehicle's travel as well?
options: About 800 feet
About 400 feet, the length of a city block
About half a mile
Over 1,600 feet (about one-third of a mile)
questions.ref: p.23 Rules of Passing: at 55 mph you travel over 800 feet in 10 seconds, and so does an oncoming vehicle, so you need over 1600 feet (about one-third of a mile).

questions.q: You are driving on a busy road and a passenger asks to be let out right away. What does the manual recommend?
options: Stop in the right travel lane with your flashers on, since a brief stop to let a passenger out is permitted
Find a safe place out of traffic to stop; never stop in a travel lane to let a passenger out
Back up along the edge of the road to the last cross street, where the passenger can get out safely
Stop in the bicycle lane for a moment, since no other traffic is using it while the passenger gets out
questions.ref: p. 24, Backing: do not stop in travel lanes for any reason (confusion, breakdown, letting out a passenger); keep moving until you can safely pull off the road. Also p. 22, Space Behind.

questions.q: You are driving toward a stopped school bus that has its red lights flashing. The bus is traveling toward you on the opposite roadway, separated from your roadway by a median. What must you do?
options: You are not required to stop; a median separates the roadways
Stop and wait until the red lights stop flashing
Slow to 10 mph and proceed with caution
Stop only if children are visible near the bus
questions.ref: p.37 Right-of-Way: you are not required to stop if the bus is traveling toward you and a median or other physical barrier separates the roadway.

questions.q: Which statement about large trucks and small underpowered cars is supported by the manual?
options: They can lose speed on long or steep hills, and it takes them longer to get up to speed when they enter traffic
They can climb steep hills faster than other vehicles, but they need extra room when they slow to enter traffic
They are required by law to use the shoulder on steep grades, so you should expect them to pull out of the lane
They keep up with the speed of traffic on grades, so you only need to watch for them at railroad crossings
questions.ref: p. 18, Slow Moving Vehicles: watch for large trucks and small underpowered cars on steep grades or when entering traffic; they can lose speed on long or steep hills and take longer to get up to speed when they enter traffic.

questions.q: A police car is stopped on the shoulder of a highway and the lane next to it is clear. What does Connecticut's Move Over Law require?
options: Keep your speed and move over one lane whenever it is safe
Slow down below the posted limit but stay in your lane regardless
Stop beside the vehicle until the officer waves you on
Slow to below the posted limit and move over one lane when safe
questions.ref: p.16 Move Over Law: when any vehicle is pulled over, slow down (below the posted speed limit) and move over one lane whenever safe.

questions.q: Connecticut's Vulnerable User's Law provides higher penalties when a driver who fails to use reasonable care seriously injures or kills a vulnerable user. Which of the following is NOT listed as a vulnerable user?
options: A highway worker
A taxi driver
A person riding or driving an animal
The driver of a garbage truck
questions.ref: p.16 Vulnerable Users: pedestrians, bicyclists, wheelchair users, people riding/driving animals, highway workers, garbage trucks, tank vehicles, mail and express delivery vehicles; taxis are not listed.

questions.q: Trucks, buses and RVs have large blind spots. Approximately how far can those blind spots stretch in front of the cab and behind the truck?
options: Up to 10 feet in front and about 100 feet behind
Up to 200 feet in front and about 20 feet behind
Up to 20 feet in front of the cab and about 200 feet behind
Up to 65 feet in front and about 400 feet behind
questions.ref: p.19 Wide Turns: blind spots may stretch up to 20 feet in front of the cab and approximately 200 feet behind the truck.

questions.q: You are traveling at 55 mph when a steady rain begins and the road becomes wet. By about how much does the manual say you should reduce your speed?
options: About 10 mph, to roughly 45 mph
About 20 mph, to roughly 35 mph
By half, to roughly 28 mph
About 5 mph, to roughly 50 mph
questions.ref: p.25 Slippery Roads: on a wet road, reduce your speed by about 10 mph (on packed snow, cut speed in half).

questions.q: Which of the following is a WARNING SIGN of fatigue rather than a recommended way to prevent a fatigue-related crash?
options: Finding a safe parking area to take a 15 to 20 minute nap
Pulling off at the next exit or rest area to find a place to sleep
Consuming the equivalent of 2 cups of coffee before taking a short nap
Turning up the radio or rolling down a window to stay awake
questions.ref: p.28 Warning Signs of Fatigue include turning up the radio or rolling down the window; prevention includes stopping, napping 15-20 minutes, and caffeine before a short nap.

questions.q: A 19-year-old is arrested for DUI and tests at .02 percent or higher. Which penalty does the manual describe?
options: License suspended at least 30 days, then an ignition interlock device for at least six months
Suspension of at least 45 days, then an ignition interlock for at least one year
License suspended at least 45 days, with an interlock device for at least six months
No suspension, because only adults are penalized at that test result
questions.ref: p.33 Alcohol and the Law: under 21, a test of .02 percent or higher means suspension of at least 45 days and an IID for at least one year (six months applies to the general failed-test case).

questions.q: Which of the following equals one alcoholic drink according to the manual?
options: An 8 oz. glass of wine
A 16 oz. mug of beer
A 5 oz. glass of wine
A 3 oz. shot of 80-proof liquor
questions.ref: p.33 Alcohol and You: an alcohol drink is 1.5 oz. of 80-proof liquor, 12 oz. of beer, or a 5 oz. glass of wine.

questions.q: Snow is falling and traffic is heavy, but you are driving exactly at the posted speed limit. Which statement is correct?
options: You cannot be ticketed, because a driver who stays at or below the posted limit is never cited for speed
You can still be ticketed; limits are posted for ideal conditions, so slow down for conditions
You can be ticketed only if a crash occurs, because the posted limit applies to all weather conditions
You can be ticketed only if you are more than 10 mph above the limit, since slippery roads allow some leeway
questions.ref: p. 36, Speed Limits: speed limits are posted for ideal conditions; if the road is wet or icy, you cannot see well, or traffic is heavy, you must slow down, and you can get a ticket for traveling too fast for conditions even at the posted limit.

questions.q: You want to park on a street near a stop sign and a fire hydrant. What minimum distances must you keep?
options: 25 feet from the stop sign and 10 feet from the fire hydrant
10 feet from the stop sign and 25 feet from the fire hydrant
25 feet from the stop sign and 25 feet from the fire hydrant
10 feet from the stop sign and 10 feet from the fire hydrant
questions.ref: p.37 No-Parking Zones: do not park within 25 feet of a stop sign or within 10 feet of a fire hydrant.

questions.q: A rectangular sign is mounted with its long side vertical. According to the manual, what do vertical rectangular signs generally give?
options: Directions or information about places
A warning about a hazard ahead on the road
Instructions or tell you the law
The location of services such as gas and rest areas
questions.ref: p. 46, Shapes, Rectangle/square: vertical signs generally give instructions or tell you the law; horizontal signs may give directions or information.

questions.q: At a HAWK pedestrian signal, the display is flashing red. What must you do?
options: Stop and remain stopped until the signal goes dark
Slow down and proceed with caution
Stop, then proceed after pedestrians have cleared the crosswalk
Stop and wait until a green light appears
questions.ref: p.45 HAWK Signals: Flashing Red means the signal is about to deactivate; drivers must stop but may proceed when pedestrians have cleared the crosswalk.

questions.q: A double solid white line on the pavement means:
options: You may change lanes only if the next lane is clear
The lane is shared with bicycles
Passing is permitted on either side
Lane changing is prohibited
questions.ref: p.44 Other Markings: a double solid white line prohibits lane changing.

questions.q: Jordan is 19 and has never held a license in any state. What must Jordan do before taking the road test?
options: Hold a permit for at least 120 days and complete 30 hours of classroom instruction
Hold a permit for at least 180 days; no course is required for adults
Hold a learner's permit for at least 90 days and present a certificate for the 8-hour safe driving course
Hold a permit for at least 30 days; the 8-hour course applies only to applicants under 18
questions.ref: p.7 Applicants 18 or Older: must hold a permit at least 90 days before the road test and, if no prior license, take an 8-hour safe driving course and show proof.

questions.q: A 16-year-old permit holder wants to practice driving. Which person may give instruction from the front passenger seat?
options: A 22-year-old who has held a license for five years with no suspension
A 19-year-old who has held a license for three years
A 21-year-old who has held a license for four years but had it suspended two years ago
A 30-year-old who has held a license for two years
questions.ref: p.6 Permit Passenger Restrictions: the instructor must be at least 20, have held a license four or more consecutive years, and not have been suspended in the prior four years.

questions.q: Under the Connecticut Teen-Parent Driver Agreement, a supervising adult agrees to do what if the teen calls for a ride to avoid a dangerous driving situation?
options: Give the ride, but count the call as a violation if the teen had broken the curfew or passenger rules
Give the ride only if the teen has not been drinking, and suspend driving privileges for the days agreed
Give the ride only during the first six months after licensing, when the teen may carry no friends as passengers
Give the teen a ride at any time and for any reason, and the call will not count as a violation of the Agreement
questions.ref: p. 30, Supervising Adult's Obligations: the adult will, at any time and for any reason, give the teen a ride to avoid a dangerous driving or other situation, and the call will not count as a violation.

questions.q: An applicant is blind in one eye. What does the manual require of the other eye?
options: Vision of at least 20/20 and a visual field of 100 degrees or more
Vision of at least 20/40 and a minimal visual field of 100 degrees or more
Vision of at least 20/40 and a visual field of 180 degrees
Vision of at least 20/30 and a visual field of 120 degrees
questions.ref: p.5 The Vision Test: minimum 20/40; if blind in one eye the other eye must be at least 20/40 with a minimal visual field of 100 degrees or more.

questions.q: A 30-year-old driver is stopped at a red light. Which action is legal under Connecticut's cell phone law?
options: Holding the phone to read a text message, since the car is stopped
Using a hands-free accessory for a phone call
Holding the phone briefly to check a map
Dialing a number on a hand-held phone because the light is red
questions.ref: p.13 Cell Phone Laws: hand-held use is prohibited even when temporarily stopped for traffic or a signal; hands-free accessories are permitted for adults.

questions.q: A 6-year-old child weighs 50 pounds. Which restraint meets the manual's requirements?
options: A rear-facing car seat only
The vehicle seat belt alone
A 5-point harness only; a booster seat is not allowed
A 5-point harness or a booster seat
questions.ref: p.12 Child Safety Requirements: age 5 to 8, or weighing between 40 and 60 pounds, requires a 5-point harness or booster seat.

questions.q: You have just installed dark tinted windows and new lighting on your car. What does the manual caution?
options: Such changes are legal anywhere as long as you keep the front windshield free of tint and the headlights aimed
Such changes are restricted only for commercial vehicles, so a passenger car may use any tint or lighting
After-market changes to equipment, such as tinted windows and lighting, may violate legal standards
Such changes are legal if you use your headlights and wipers together, as the law requires in the rain
questions.ref: p. 12, Interior Equipment note: after market changes to equipment such as tinted windows and lighting may violate legal standards (Study Question 2).

questions.q: You move into the middle of a four-second opening in traffic when merging. What following distance do you and the vehicle behind you each have?
options: Three seconds
Four seconds
Two seconds
One second
questions.ref: p.20 Space to Merge: in the middle of a four-second opening, both you and the vehicle behind have a two-second following distance.

questions.q: A driver is following you very closely, and the road has no right lane to move into. What does the manual recommend?
options: Brake quickly and firmly to make the driver back off
Speed up until you gain more space
Wait until the road ahead is clear, then slowly reduce speed
Pull onto the shoulder and stop until the driver has gone by you
questions.ref: p.22 Being Tailgated: if there is no right lane, wait until the road ahead is clear, then reduce speed slowly; never slow down quickly to discourage a tailgater.

questions.q: Your view ahead is blocked by a hill. Which statement is consistent with the manual?
options: Assume an oncoming vehicle is just out of sight and do not pass within one-third of a mile
Pass only if the road has a dashed yellow center line, since that marking allows passing here
Sound your horn and pass if no vehicle has appeared
Do not start to pass within 400 feet of the hill, the distance needed to stop at 50 mph
questions.ref: p.24 Hills and Curves: assume there is an oncoming vehicle just out of sight; do not start to pass if within one-third of a mile of a hill or curve.

questions.q: Your direction of travel has two lanes. According to Connecticut law, which lane should you use?
options: The left lane, which is meant for through traffic
The right lane, except when passing, making a left turn, or exiting on the left
Either lane, as long as you keep pace with traffic
The left lane whenever traffic ahead in the right lane is slower
questions.ref: p.23 Passing, Multi-Lane roads: when your direction of travel is less than three lanes, you must drive in the right lane except when passing.

questions.q: At an intersection with no painted crosswalk, a pedestrian at the curb pushes a stroller into the entrance of the crosswalk. What must you do?
options: Proceed, since a crosswalk without painted lines has no legal status
Proceed, because the pedestrian has not yet entered the roadway
Sound your horn to alert the pedestrian and continue slowly
Slow or stop and yield, because every intersection has a crosswalk
questions.ref: p.16 Pedestrians: there is a crosswalk at every intersection even if unmarked; yield when a pedestrian moves any extension of the body, including a stroller, into the crosswalk entrance.

questions.q: You pass a bicyclist, and the intersection where you plan to turn right is just ahead. What should you do?
options: Slow down and let the bicyclist clear the intersection before you turn
Turn right immediately; the bicyclist is now behind you
Sound your horn, then turn right ahead of the bicyclist
Move into the bike lane to make your turn
questions.ref: p.17 Bicyclists: you must not pass a bicyclist immediately before a right turn; slow down and let the cyclist clear the intersection before turning.

questions.q: An approaching motorcycle has its left turn signal flashing but has not slowed, and you want to turn left across its path. What should you do?
options: Turn now, since a flashing signal always means it will turn before reaching you
Flash your headlights and turn
Wait until it actually begins to turn
Turn if there is room, because motorcycle signals cancel themselves
questions.ref: p.18 Motorcycles: do not assume a motorcycle is turning because its signal flashes; signals may not self-cancel. Do not pull out until it actually begins to turn.

questions.q: You are driving toward a person riding a horse along the road. Which action is ILLEGAL?
options: Reducing your speed
Stopping if necessary
Passing at a reasonable speed and distance
Sounding your horn or making loud or unusual noises
questions.ref: p.18 Horses: you must reduce speed (or stop), drive at a reasonable speed and distance; it is illegal to sound your horn or cause loud or unusual noises.

questions.q: An emergency vehicle with its siren on approaches from behind while you are in the middle of an intersection. What should you do?
options: Stop where you are in the middle of the intersection and wait for it to pass you
Drive through the intersection, then pull over to the right and stop
Pull to the left so it can pass on the right
Brake and back out of the intersection
questions.ref: p.37 Right-of-Way: if you are in an intersection, drive through the intersection before you pull over.

questions.q: Which statement about slippery roads is TRUE according to the manual?
options: Ice is less slippery when the temperature is right around freezing than when it is well below freezing
Shady spots on cold, wet days dry out first and are the last places to freeze
Pavement is safest during the first few minutes of rain on a hot day
Bridges can be icy even when other pavement is not, since no earth insulates them
questions.ref: p.25 Slippery Roads: bridges can be colder and icier; ice is more slippery near freezing; shady spots freeze first and dry last; hot-day rain makes pavement slippery at first.

questions.q: A hostile driver follows you after an angry exchange. What does the manual say to do?
options: Do not make eye contact, and drive to a police station or other public, well-lit location
Drive home so the person cannot hurt anyone else
Pull over and speak calmly with the other driver
Make eye contact to show you are not afraid
questions.ref: p.26 Eye Contact: do not make eye contact; if a motorist pursues you, do not go home but drive to a police station, convenience store or other public well-lit location.

questions.q: Which statement about Connecticut's ignition interlock device (IID) requirement for adult drivers is correct?
options: Both failing and refusing the test require an IID for at least six months or more
An adult who refuses the test needs an IID for six months, but one who fails needs it for a year
Failing the test means an IID for at least six months; refusing means at least one year
An adult who refuses the test faces only a 45-day suspension and no ignition interlock
questions.ref: p.33 Alcohol and the Law: failing the test means an IID for at least six months; regardless of age, refusing means an IID for at least one year.

questions.q: You need to take an over-the-counter allergy medicine before driving. What does the manual advise?
options: Take it, because over-the-counter drugs do not affect driving
Check the label for warnings, and ask your doctor or pharmacist if you are unsure it is safe to drive
Take it with coffee to offset any drowsiness
Take half the dose, which will not affect your reflexes
questions.ref: p.33 Drugs and Driving: drugs for allergies can make a person drowsy; check the label and ask your doctor or pharmacist if you are not sure.

questions.q: You are inside a roundabout and a car waits to enter from another approach. What should you do?
options: Keep moving; do not stop in the roundabout to let that car enter
Stop inside the roundabout to let the entering car go in ahead of you
Stop at the next exit and wait for the entering car to pass
Speed up so you exit before the car enters
questions.ref: p.37 Roundabouts: entering traffic yields to circulating traffic; do not stop within the roundabout to allow traffic to enter from another leg.

questions.q: Under Connecticut law, when must you turn on your headlights?
options: Only after sunset
Only when it is snowing or foggy
Only when driving on roads without street lights
Whenever you turn on your windshield wipers
questions.ref: p.38 Use Headlights: if you turn on your wipers, turn on your headlights; it's the law.

questions.q: A sign with a fluorescent yellow-green background is most likely to warn you about:
options: Construction or maintenance work
Services such as gas stations or hospitals
Pedestrians, bicyclists, or a school area
Parks and recreational areas
questions.ref: p.47 Colors: fluorescent yellow-green may be used for pedestrian, bicycle, and school warning signs (orange is construction, blue services, brown parks).

questions.q: You are waiting to turn left and the signal changes from a green arrow to a yellow arrow. What does this mean?
options: The signal is about to turn green, so proceed with the turn
The protection of the green arrow is ending, so prepare to stop
You may turn only if no pedestrians are present
You must stop immediately where you are, even in the intersection
questions.ref: p.45 Arrows: a yellow arrow means the protection of a green arrow is ending; if turning in the direction of the arrow, prepare to stop.

questions.q: What does a dashed yellow line alongside a solid yellow line in the center of a road indicate?
options: Passing is permitted on the side of the broken line, not the solid line
Passing is permitted from both sides of the road as long as it is safe
Passing is prohibited from both sides of the center line in all cases
It is a shared center lane for left turns from both directions
questions.ref: p.44 Center Lines: a dashed yellow line alongside a solid yellow line indicates passing is permitted on the side of the broken line, but not on the side of the solid line.

questions.q: A parent or legal guardian of a 16-year-old who gets a learner's permit must complete which training?
options: Four hours of instruction with the teen on the effects of alcohol and drug use
The full 40 hours of behind-the-wheel training with the teen
A 30-hour classroom course alongside the teen
Two hours of instruction with the teen on teen driving laws and dangers
questions.ref: p.6 Parent Training Requirements: a parent or legal guardian must complete two hours of instruction with the teen on the laws for drivers under 18 and the dangers of teen driving.

questions.q: Home training may be done by a parent, grandparent, foster parent or legal guardian, or the spouse of a married minor. Which of these may provide home training only when the applicant has none of those people, and if the person is qualified?
options: A grandparent
A brother or sister
A foster parent or legal guardian
The spouse of a married minor applicant
questions.ref: p.6 Home Training Program: if the applicant has none of the primary list, a qualified uncle or aunt, brother or sister, or stepparent may provide home training.

questions.q: A 16-year-old permit holder takes a lesson from a licensed instructor at a commercial driving school, and another student rides along with the instructor. How do the permit passenger restrictions apply?
options: Not permitted; the only passenger allowed is one person who is at least 20 years old
Permitted only if the other student is also a permit holder of the same age
Both are permitted: an instructor and others accompanying that instructor
Not permitted; the permit holder may carry no passengers except a parent
questions.ref: p.6 Permit Passenger Restrictions: exceptions include a licensed driving instructor giving instruction and others accompanying that instructor.

questions.q: A licensed 16-year-old is convicted of speeding 20 mph over the limit for the first time. What suspension does DMV impose?
options: 60 days
30 days
90 days
6 months
questions.ref: p.34 suspension table: speeding (20 mph over) is a 60-day suspension for a first offense, 90 days for a second, 6 months for a third.

questions.q: A driver and the front-seat passenger are both stopped without wearing seat belts. What can happen?
options: Only the driver can be cited, with a $75 fine
Each could be cited and fined $175
Each receives only a warning for a first offense
Each could be cited and fined $75
questions.ref: p.12 Seat Belt Laws: if either the driver or the passenger fails to wear a seat belt, each could be cited for a violation and fined $75.

questions.q: A friend sits in a parked car with the engine running for a long time while waiting. What does the manual advise?
options: Open a window; leaking exhaust gases can be deadly very quickly
Close the windows and run the heater on recirculate
Nothing special; exhaust gases are only a danger inside a closed garage
Keep the doors locked and the engine running for security
questions.ref: p.12 Exhaust System: if you sit in a vehicle with the motor running for a long time, open a window; never run the motor in a closed garage.

questions.q: A 17-year-old driver talks to a friend using a hands-free device and is convicted of violating the cell phone law. What is the result?
options: No violation, since hands-free devices are permitted for all drivers
A fine only, with no license suspension for a first conviction of the cell phone law
It is a moving violation, and the conviction results in a license suspension
A violation only if the vehicle is moving faster than 25 mph
questions.ref: p.13 Cell Phone Laws: 16- and 17-year-olds may not use any device, even hands-free; a conviction under 18 results in license suspension and counts as a moving violation.

questions.q: You are following a car and pass the same sign two seconds after the rear of that car passed it. What does the manual say to do?
options: Nothing, because two seconds is a safe following distance at any speed
Drop back and recount at another spot until you are no closer than three seconds
Speed up so that you pass the car and no longer follow it
Drop back to exactly four seconds, which is the required distance on dry roads
questions.ref: p.21 Space Ahead: if you pass the mark before finishing the count you are following too closely; drop back and recount until following no closer than three seconds.

questions.q: Before you change into the next lane on a road with several lanes in your direction, what else does the manual say to check besides the lane you want to enter?
options: The shoulder, because a vehicle parked there may pull back onto the road and take the lane you want to enter
The far lane, because someone in that lane may be planning to move into the same lane you want to enter
The oncoming lanes, because a driver there may cross over into the lane that you are planning to enter
The lane behind you only, because traffic in the far lane cannot possibly reach the lane you want to enter
questions.ref: p. 23, Changing Lanes: check the far lane (if there is one), as someone in that lane may be planning to move into the same lane that you want to enter.

questions.q: A freight train has just cleared a crossing that has more than one track. What should you do before crossing?
options: Cross immediately, since the train that passed has already cleared the crossing area
Look only in the direction the train came from, then cross when it is clear
Stop on the tracks for a moment to look carefully in both directions
Wait until the passing train is well down the track, since it may hide a second train
questions.ref: p.15 Railroad Crossings: at crossings with more than one track, wait until the passing train is well down the track; the train that just passed may hide another one.

questions.q: Signs in a work zone warn that your lane ends ahead. What does the manual advise?
options: Merge as soon as possible, at first notice of the approaching work zone
Stay in the closing lane to the end, then take turns merging
Speed up to pass slower vehicles before the lane ends
Stop before the lane closure until a flagger waves you ahead
questions.ref: p.16 Work Zones: merge as soon as possible; move to the appropriate lane at first notice of an approaching work zone.

questions.q: You are about to overtake a bicyclist on a narrow road when a vehicle approaches from the opposite direction. What should you do?
options: Speed up and pass before the vehicles meet, leaving as much room as you can for the bicyclist
Sound your horn to warn the bicyclist, then pass while the oncoming car approaches
Slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass first, then give the bicyclist three feet
Pass with at least one foot of clearance, since the oncoming car limits your space
questions.ref: p.22 Space to the Side: take hazards one at a time; slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass first, and allow at least three feet when passing a bicycle.

questions.q: A bike lane runs along the curb and you are about to turn right. What is the correct way to handle the turn?
options: Merge into the bike lane early so you are next to the curb for the turn
Yield to bicyclists, then turn across the lane without driving in it beforehand
Turn from the travel lane without checking, since bicyclists must yield to turning vehicles
Drive in the bike lane for the last half block, then turn
questions.ref: p.17 Bicyclists: you must yield to bicycles in the bike lane; you may turn across a bicycle lane but may not drive in it when approaching a turn.

questions.q: A tractor-trailer is approaching an intersection with its right turn signal on, and you are in the lane to its right. What should you do?
options: Do not pass on its right, or you could be caught between the truck and the curb
Pass on the right quickly before the truck starts its turn
Move up beside its rear wheels, since rear wheels follow a shorter path than the front wheels
Stay alongside the cab so the driver can see you in the side mirror
questions.ref: p.20 Trucks Make Wide Right Turns: resist the temptation to pass on the right of a truck approaching an intersection; you could be caught between the truck and the curb.

questions.q: You are about to back out of your driveway. Why does the manual say to be extra watchful?
options: Delivery vehicles are required to stop behind your vehicle so that the driver has a clear view of the road ahead
Pedestrians on the sidewalk are required to wait until your vehicle has fully entered the road
Other drivers on the road must give you the right-of-way because you are entering from a driveway
Children may run behind or be playing behind your vehicle, where you cannot see them from the driver's seat
questions.ref: p. 16, Children at Play and School Zones: always be extra watchful when backing in or out of a driveway; children may run behind or be playing behind your vehicle.

questions.q: An orange triangle on the back of a vehicle identifies it as:
options: A vehicle carrying hazardous materials
A school bus that is about to stop
A slow-moving vehicle, such as a farm tractor, usually going 25 mph or less
A vehicle that is required to stop at railroad crossings
questions.ref: p.18 Slow Moving Vehicles: farm tractors, animal-drawn and roadway maintenance vehicles usually go 25 mph or less and should have a slow-moving decal (an orange triangle).

questions.q: Heavy rain begins and it feels like your tires have lost traction with the road. What should you do?
options: Ease off the gas and keep the wheel straight until the tires grip again
Brake hard and steer toward the shoulder as quickly as you can to get off the road
Steer sharply back and forth to regain grip on the wet pavement
Accelerate gently to power through the water until traction returns
questions.ref: p.25 Water on the Roadway: ease your foot off the gas, keep the wheel straight, and do not try to stop or turn until your tires are gripping the road again.

questions.q: You feel very angry after an argument and need to drive somewhere. What does the manual suggest?
options: Turn up the radio, since music helps when you are angry or excited
Give yourself time to cool off, such as a short walk or nap, before driving
Take a longer route so that the extra time on the road helps you calm down
Drive in the left lane, away from other traffic, until the anger passes
questions.ref: p.28 Emotions: if you are angry or excited, give yourself time to cool off and stay off the road until calm (listening to the radio is suggested for being worried or down).

questions.q: Which driver would be REQUIRED to complete the DMV-certified operator retraining program?
options: A 22-year-old with one moving violation
A 30-year-old with two moving violations
A 25-year-old with two moving violations
A 22-year-old with two moving violations
questions.ref: p.35 Operator Retraining: age 24 or younger with two or more moving violations must complete it; age 25 or older requires three or more convictions.

questions.q: After a night of drinking, a driver says a cold shower and several cups of coffee will sober him up. According to the manual:
options: Coffee will help, but only when combined with fresh air
A cold shower will help after about 30 minutes
Time is the only thing that will sober you up
Exercise will lower his blood alcohol content within an hour
questions.ref: p.33 Alcohol and You: there is no way to sober up quickly; coffee, fresh air, exercise, or cold showers will not help; time is the only thing.

questions.q: On a dry road with good tires and brakes, you can see only 300 feet ahead. According to the manual's stopping distances, which speed may be unsafe?
options: 30 mph
50 mph
25 mph
20 mph
questions.ref: p.36 How Well Can You See: about 400 feet to stop at 50 mph and about 200 feet at 30 mph; if you cannot see 400 feet ahead you may not be driving safely at 50 mph.

questions.q: You intend to turn into a driveway just beyond an intersection. When should you signal?
options: Wait until you reach the intersection, then signal
Signal as soon as you can see the driveway
Signal one full block before the intersection so drivers behind you have time
Do not signal; driveways do not require a signal
questions.ref: p.39 Turn Signals: if there are streets, driveways, or intersections between you and where you want to turn, wait until you have reached that point before signaling.

questions.q: You are approaching a railroad crossing you have never seen a train use before. What does the manual advise?
options: Keep your normal speed and watch only for flashing lights or gates, because a crossing where you have never seen a train is rarely used
Slow down and look only in the direction of the nearest approaching traffic, since trains travel with traffic
Slow down and look up and down the tracks, because assuming no train is coming is one of the leading causes of fatalities at crossings
Stop and shift to a lower gear before the tracks so that you do not have to shift while crossing
questions.ref: p. 15, Railroad Crossings: slow down and look up and down the tracks; even if you have never seen a train at that crossing, do not assume none are coming, one of the leading causes of fatalities.

questions.q: A steady yellow X is displayed over a reversible lane you are driving in. What does it mean?
options: The lane may be used only for turning
The lane is open to you, so continue
The lane is closed and you must stop at once
Use of the lane is changing; move out of it when safe
questions.ref: p.44 Reversible Lanes: a steady yellow X means use of the lane is changing and you should move out as soon as safe (a flashing yellow X means turning only).

questions.q: Connecticut freeway mileposts are placed every mile. Where does zero usually start?
options: At the south and west borders of the state
At the north and east borders of the state
At Hartford
At the south and east borders of the state
questions.ref: p.51 Destination and Distance Signs: mileposts are placed every mile; zero usually starts at the south and west borders of the state.

questions.q: Which applicant must complete the 8-hour Safe Driving Practices course before getting a Connecticut license?
options: A 40-year-old who has never held a license in any state
A 40-year-old who holds a valid license issued by another state
An 18-year-old who previously held a Connecticut license
A 45-year-old Connecticut resident renewing a valid license
questions.ref: p.4 and p.7: anyone who has not previously held a license in Connecticut or does not hold a valid license from another state must take the 8-hour Safe Driving Practices course.

questions.q: Which statement about the road test is TRUE?
options: A permit holder may drive alone to the test location if the vehicle is registered
An applicant without a valid license may use a rented vehicle if the rental is fully insured
If the vehicle is unsafe, no test is given and the applicant reschedules for no fee
A long-term leased vehicle may be used without proof of insurance since the lessor owns it
questions.ref: p.7 The Road Test: an unsafe vehicle means no evaluation and a no-fee reschedule; a non-licensed operator cannot drive to the test alone; no rented vehicle without a valid license; leased vehicles need proof of insurance.

questions.q: A 16-year-old licensed driver is convicted of a second violation of a Graduated Driver's License restriction, such as the curfew. What suspension applies?
options: 30 days
6 months, or until age 18, whichever is longer
90 days
1 year
questions.ref: p.34 suspension table: GDL violations are 30 days for a first offense and 6 months or until age 18, whichever is longer, for second and subsequent offenses.

questions.q: A limited driver's license has a restriction allowing driving only 'during the period of daylight.' What does the manual say that means?
options: From exactly sunrise to exactly sunset, with no extra time
From one full hour before sunrise to one full hour after sunset
From 5 a.m. until the 11 p.m. curfew begins
From half an hour before sunrise to half an hour after sunset
questions.ref: p.9 Limited Licenses: restriction to daylight begins half an hour before sunrise and ends half an hour after sunset.

questions.q: Which statement about underinflated or unbalanced tires is correct?
options: They wear the tires evenly but reduce fuel economy a little
They improve traction on wet roads while reducing fuel economy
They cause faster tire wear, lower fuel economy, and harder steering and stopping
They affect only fuel economy and have no effect on steering or stopping distance
questions.ref: p.11 Tires: unbalanced tires and low pressure cause faster tire wear, reduce fuel economy, and make the vehicle harder to steer and stop.

questions.q: What adjustment does the manual suggest for your side mirrors?
options: Set them so that when you lean forward slightly, you can see the side of your vehicle
Set them so you can see the side of your vehicle while sitting upright without leaning
Angle them inward so they show the same view as the rear view mirror
Set them to show only the road behind your rear bumper
questions.ref: p.12 Mirrors: a good adjustment for the side mirrors is to set them so that when you lean forward slightly, you can see the side of your vehicle.

questions.q: Which driver may legally use a hand-held cell phone while driving?
options: A 30-year-old driver stopped at a red light
A 22-year-old using it only at a stop sign
A 50-year-old driver calling a friend to say he is on his way
A 35-year-old peace officer
questions.ref: p.13 Cell Phone Laws: drivers 18 and older who are peace officers, firefighters, or ambulance drivers may use hand-held phones; use is also barred when temporarily stopped.

questions.q: You are stopped at a stop sign and parked vehicles block your view of the cross street. What should you do?
options: Pull forward quickly to look past the vehicles
Edge forward slowly until you can see
Wait for the driver in the next lane to go first
Sound your horn and proceed slowly
questions.ref: p.15 Intersections: if your view of a cross street is blocked, edge forward slowly until you can see so crossing drivers can see the front of your vehicle.

questions.q: While passing, when does the manual say it is safe to return to your lane?
options: When both headlights of the passed vehicle show in your rear-view mirror
As soon as your front bumper is even with the passed vehicle's rear bumper
When you have counted three seconds after passing
When the passed vehicle's roof appears in your rear-view mirror
questions.ref: p.23 Return to your lane: when you can see both headlights of the vehicle you just passed in your rear-view mirror, it is safe to return.

questions.q: You are on a multi-lane road and realize you are beside and slightly behind another vehicle. What should you do?
options: Stay in position, since driving beside a vehicle gives you the most room
Sound your horn to warn the other driver
Speed up or drop back so the other driver can see you more easily
Move closer to the vehicle so it sees you in its mirror
questions.ref: p.22 Blind Spots: avoid driving on either side and slightly to the rear of another vehicle; speed up or drop back so the other driver can see you.

questions.q: Where should your hands be placed on the steering wheel according to the manual?
options: Left hand between 10 and 12 o'clock and right hand between 12 and 2 o'clock
Both hands at the top of the wheel, between 11 and 1 o'clock
Left hand between 4 and 6 o'clock and right hand between 6 and 8 o'clock
Left hand between 8 and 10 o'clock and right hand between 2 and 4 o'clock
questions.ref: p.14 Steering: both hands on opposite sides of the wheel, left hand between 8 and 10 o'clock and right hand between 2 and 4 o'clock.

questions.q: When is a driver permitted to pass in a no-passing zone?
options: When passing any vehicle that is traveling below the posted speed limit on that road
When passing a slow-moving vehicle or bicycle and you can see far enough ahead
When no oncoming vehicle is in sight and the road ahead looks clear
When the driver behind you is honking or flashing headlights at you
questions.ref: p.18 Slow Moving Vehicles: state law permits passing slow moving traffic, pedestrians, parked or standing vehicles, animals, bicycles, mopeds and scooters in no-passing zones if you can see far enough ahead to pass safely.

questions.q: Why does the manual tell drivers to be especially alert for elderly and disabled pedestrians?
options: They are not covered by right-of-way rules in crosswalks, so drivers must proceed first and let them cross behind
They are required to cross only at painted crosswalks, and drivers can expect them to stay within those lines
They may have poor vision and hearing and may move slowly, and they are among the most frequent victims in auto-pedestrian collisions
They often use white canes, so drivers should sound the horn to alert them before passing
questions.ref: p. 16, Pedestrians: be especially alert for children, the elderly and disabled pedestrians; they are the most frequent victims, and elderly and disabled pedestrians may have poor vision and hearing and may move slowly.

questions.q: According to the manual, nearly 40 percent of motorcycle crashes with another vehicle were caused by the other vehicle doing what?
options: Turning left in front of the motorcyclist
Following the motorcycle too closely in heavy traffic
Changing lanes without signaling or checking mirrors
Backing out of a driveway into the motorcyclist's lane
questions.ref: p.18 Motorcycles: nearly 40 percent were caused by the other vehicle turning left in front of the motorcyclist.

questions.q: You see a truck driver attempting to back from the street into a loading area. What should you do?
options: Drive around the truck quickly on the left
Stop to give the driver a chance to back up safely
Sound your horn so the driver sees you
Slow down and drive around it, staying close to its rear
questions.ref: p.20 Trucks Need Space While Backing Up: stop to give them a chance; never attempt to drive around a backing truck.

questions.q: Which is a correct practice when getting out of a vehicle parked at the curb?
options: Get out on the street side so you can watch oncoming traffic
Open the door before checking, since other drivers must avoid it
Leave the door open while you unload, so others will see it
Check traffic first and, if you can, get out on the curb side
questions.ref: p.37 Parking: check traffic before you open the door; get out on the curbside if you can; shut the door as soon as you can after getting out.

questions.q: When are studded tires permitted in Connecticut?
options: From October 1st through March 31st
From December 1st through March 15th
From November 15th through April 30th
All year, if the driver needs them for ice
questions.ref: p.25 Slippery Roads: studded tires are permitted in Connecticut from November 15th through April 30th.

questions.q: During a long trip, your tires pass over a shoulder rumble strip. What should you do?
options: Pull off at a safe place immediately and check your alertness
Turn up the radio and continue to the next exit
Steer back into the lane and continue, because the strip did its job
Drive faster to reach your destination before fatigue gets worse
questions.ref: p.28 Rumble strips: if you run over a shoulder rumble strip, pull off the road at a safe place immediately and check your alertness level.

questions.q: A 17-year-old commits one of the following offenses. Which one CANNOT be considered under youthful offender status?
options: Reckless driving, even without any crash
Street racing on a public highway
Operating a vehicle while under suspension
Driving under the influence (DUI)
questions.ref: p.35 Youthful Offender Status: someone under 18 who commits negligent homicide, evades responsibility after a death or serious injury, or drives under the influence cannot be a youthful offender.

questions.q: You are pulled over by a police vehicle at night. Which action does the manual recommend?
options: Get out and walk back to the officer's vehicle with your license in hand
Turn on the interior light after stopping, before the officer approaches
Reach for your license and registration as the officer approaches
Turn off all lights, including the interior light, to avoid glare
questions.ref: p.35 Stopping for Police Vehicles: if at night, turn on the interior light after stopping and before the officer approaches; get license and registration only when requested; remain in the vehicle.

questions.q: Which describes the correct way to make a legal U-turn?
options: Give a right turn signal and finish in the left lane nearest the median
Make it from the right lane without signaling
Give a left turn signal, stop, check for approaching traffic, then proceed into the outside (right-hand) lane traveling the opposite way
Make it at an opening in the median of an expressway
questions.ref: p.37 U-Turns: never make a U-turn on an expressway; give a left turn signal, stop, check traffic, and proceed into the outside or right-hand lane in the opposite direction.

questions.q: Your gas pedal sticks and the engine keeps going faster and faster. After keeping your eyes on the road, what should you do first?
options: Turn the ignition key to the 'lock' position
Quickly shift to neutral
Pull the parking brake handle all the way up
Pump the brake pedal several times
questions.ref: p.40 Gas Pedal Sticks: keep your eyes on the road, quickly shift to neutral, pull off the road when safe, then turn off the engine; never turn the ignition to 'lock' while moving.

questions.q: A center lane is marked on each side by a solid yellow line and a dashed yellow line, with left-turn arrows alternating from each direction. What is it?
options: A reversible lane that carries traffic one way at certain times of the day
A passing lane shared by traffic in either direction
An HOV lane for vehicles with more than one person
A shared center lane for left turns or U-turns, used by both directions
questions.ref: p.44 Shared Center Lane: reserved for left turns or permitted U-turns by vehicles traveling in both directions; marked by solid and dashed yellow lines on each side.

questions.q: Which is correct about turning right at a red light?
