options: You may turn after coming to a full stop and checking for oncoming traffic, unless a sign prohibits the turn
You may turn without stopping if no pedestrians are present
You may turn only where a sign specifically permits it
You may turn only after the red light changes to yellow
questions.ref: p.45 Red lights: you may turn right on red after a full stop and checking for oncoming traffic and no sign prohibiting it; also p.15 you may turn right at a red light after stopping unless prohibited.

questions.q: A 'Wrong Way' sign is used to identify:
options: The beginning of a detour around a closed road
A lane that is reserved for turning vehicles
The point where a divided highway begins
A one-way street, expressway ramp, or the wrong side of a divided highway; do not drive past it, turn around
questions.ref: p.47 Wrong Way: used to identify a one-way street, expressway ramp or the wrong direction or wrong side of a divided highway; do not drive past this sign, turn around.

questions.q: A 16-year-old is being home trained and must show a course completion certificate from an approved eight-hour course. At least how many of those hours must cover alcohol and drugs, the dangers of driving after using them, and the related penalties?
options: Two hours, matching the length of the parent training class
Six hours, leaving two hours for the parent training class
Four hours, as part of the approved eight-hour course
All eight hours, because the course is devoted to the topic
questions.ref: p.6 Home Training Program: the CS-1 a certificate must come from an approved eight-hour course that includes a minimum of four hours on the effects of alcohol and drugs, the dangers of driving after consuming them, and the related penalties.

questions.q: Nine months after receiving her license, a 16-year-old driver wants to carry a passenger. Which passenger is allowed in addition to those permitted during her first six months?
options: Her younger brother, a member of her immediate family
Her best friend, who is a licensed 17-year-old
A neighbor who is 20 years old and has held a license for two years
A cousin who is 19 years old
questions.ref: p.8 Passenger Restrictions: during months seven through twelve the only additional passengers allowed are members of the driver's immediate family.

questions.q: A parent asks when a newly licensed teen is at the greatest risk of a crash. According to the DMV Commissioner's Advisory Committee on Teen Safe Driving, which period is the most dangerous?
options: The second six months, when immediate family passengers are first allowed
The month after the teen turns 18, when the restrictions end
The first month of holding a learner's permit, before any supervised practice
The first six months after the teen first receives a driver's license
questions.ref: p.4 Managing Your Teen's Driving Experience: most teen crashes occur during the first two years of having a license, and the first six months are the most dangerous for the newly licensed teen.

questions.q: A 17-year-old with a learner's permit wants to practice driving. Which passenger arrangement is permitted?
options: An 18-year-old friend who has held a license for one year, sitting in the front seat
One person providing instruction, age 21, with an unsuspended license held for six straight years
Two friends, as long as there is a seat belt for each of them and one is a licensed driver
A 19-year-old sibling who has held a driver's license for five consecutive years
questions.ref: pp.5-6 Learner's Permit Passenger Restrictions: only a licensed instructor, or one person providing instruction who is at least 20 years old, has held a license four or more consecutive years and had no suspension in that period.

questions.q: A driver is wearing a seat belt, but the passenger in the back seat is not. A police officer stops the car. What may happen?
options: Both the driver and the passenger could be cited, with a fine of $75
Only the passenger can be cited
No one can be cited because the driver is buckled
Only the driver can be cited because he is responsible for the passengers
questions.ref: p.12 Connecticut Seat Belt Laws: if either the driver or the passenger fails to wear the seat belt, each could be cited for a seat belt violation and fined $75.

questions.q: A 17-year-old driver is stopped at a red light and uses a hands-free earpiece to talk to a friend. Under Connecticut law, this is:
options: Legal, because the device is hands-free
Legal, because the vehicle is temporarily stopped
Illegal, because drivers under 18 may not use any cell phone, even hands-free
Legal, as long as the call lasts less than two minutes
questions.ref: p.13 Cell Phone Laws: drivers who are 16 or 17 are not permitted to use any type of cell phone or mobile electronic device, including a hands-free device.

questions.q: In the 'penny test' for tire wear, the tread is considered safe when:
options: All of Lincoln's head is visible above the tread
Lincoln's head is visible and the tires were balanced within the last month
You can read the date on the penny
Any part of Lincoln's head is covered by the tread
questions.ref: p.11 Tires: if any part of Lincoln's head is covered by the tread, you are driving with the safe amount of tread.

questions.q: You are being tailgated on a two-lane road, and there is no right lane to move into. What does the manual say to do?
options: Brake sharply so the tailgater backs off and you regain your space cushion
Wait until the road ahead is clear, then reduce speed slowly so the tailgater drives around you
Speed up to stay ahead of the tailgater until you reach a road with a right lane
Pull onto the shoulder and stop until the tailgater has driven past you
questions.ref: p.22 Being Tailgated: if there is no right lane, wait until the road ahead is clear, then reduce speed slowly; never slow down quickly to discourage a tailgater.

questions.q: You judge that the gap in the next lane is a four-second opening and you merge into the middle of it. What following distance will you and the vehicle behind you each have?
options: One second
Three seconds
Two seconds
Four seconds
questions.ref: p.20 Space to Merge: if you move into the middle of a four-second opening, both you and the vehicle behind you have a two-second following distance.

questions.q: You are driving on a road with three lanes in your direction, with a lot of traffic entering and exiting at nearby ramps, and you are not passing. Which lane does the manual suggest?
options: The center travel lane
The left-most lane, which is intended for passing slower vehicles
The right lane, so you are closest to the ramps
The shoulder, to give entering vehicles room to merge
questions.ref: p.20 Other Hints: on a road with three or more lanes in the same direction, use the center travel lane if there is a lot of entering or exiting traffic; never drive on the shoulder unless told to by officials.

questions.q: You want to pass a slow vehicle on a two-lane road. According to the manual, you should NOT start to pass if you are within how far of a hill or curve?
options: 200 feet
400 feet
One-quarter mile
One-third of a mile
questions.ref: p.24 Hills and Curves: you should not start to pass if you are within one-third of a mile of a hill or curve.

questions.q: You are in the lane next to an ice cream truck that has flashing lights and its stop signal arm and crossing arm extended. No barrier separates the lanes. What must you do?
options: Stop at least 25 feet away, then continue at normal speed once the children have cleared
Stop at least 10 feet away, then pass at 5 mph or less, yielding to crossing pedestrians
Slow to 15 mph and pass while sounding your horn to warn children near the truck
Stop at least 20 feet away, then pass at up to 10 mph, yielding to any pedestrians
questions.ref: p.18 Ice Cream Trucks: stop at least 10 feet from the front or back of the truck; after stopping you may proceed at a reasonable speed, up to 5 mph, yielding to pedestrians.

questions.q: You are about to enter a loading-dock driveway when a tractor-trailer begins backing from the street into the loading area, partly blocking your lane. What should you do?
options: Drive quickly around the rear of the truck
Tap your horn to warn the driver
Stop and give the truck driver a chance to back in safely
Pull close to the truck's cab so the driver can see you
questions.ref: p.20 Trucks Need Space While Backing Up: if you see a truck driver attempting to back, stop to give them a chance; never attempt to drive around a backing truck.

questions.q: You are driving through a neighborhood. Which of the following is NOT one of the places where the manual says to take extra care for children, who are often the least predictable pedestrians?
options: Near car washes and gas station pumps
Near schools and school bus stops where children wait
Near playgrounds and parks where children gather
Near ice cream trucks, where children cross to buy treats
questions.ref: p.16 Children at Play and School Zones: take extra care to look out for children, especially near schools, bus stops, playgrounds, parks and ice cream trucks; car washes and gas stations are not listed.

questions.q: Connecticut's Vulnerable User's Law provides higher penalties for drivers who fail to use reasonable care and cause serious injury or death to a vulnerable user. Which of the following is NOT listed as a vulnerable user?
options: A person riding or driving an animal
A highway worker
A wheelchair user
A taxi driver
questions.ref: p.16 Vulnerable Users: list includes pedestrians, bicyclists, wheelchair users, a person riding or driving an animal, highway workers, garbage trucks, tank vehicles, mail vehicles and express delivery carriers; taxis are not listed.

questions.q: A driver fails to yield the right-of-way to a bicyclist in an intersection and is cited. How does Connecticut treat the fine?
options: The fine is the same as for failing to yield to any other vehicle on the road
The fine is doubled for failure to yield the right-of-way to a bicyclist
The fine is waived if the bicyclist was not injured in the incident
The fine is doubled only if the bicyclist is under 16 years of age
questions.ref: p.17 Bicyclists, As a driver: fines are doubled for failure to yield right-of-way to a bicyclist.

questions.q: During a heavy rain at highway speed, you feel your tires lose traction with the road. What should you do?
options: Ease off the gas, keep the wheel straight, and do not brake or turn until the tires grip
Brake firmly to slow down as quickly as possible before the water gets deeper
Steer sharply toward the shoulder to get out of the standing water quickly
Accelerate gently to power through the water and regain traction
questions.ref: p.25 Water on the Roadway: if tires lose traction, ease off the gas, keep the steering wheel straight, and do not try to stop or turn until the tires grip the road again.

questions.q: On a long drive you notice you are yawning repeatedly, drifting from your lane, and missing signs. What is the best response?
options: Turn up the radio and roll down the window
Drink several cups of coffee and keep driving
Find a safe parking area and take a 15 to 20 minute nap
Keep driving until your next scheduled break, about two hours away
questions.ref: p.28 Ways to Prevent a Fatigue-Related Crash: stop driving; take a 15 to 20 minute nap in a safe parking area; turning up the radio or opening a window is itself a warning sign, and caffeine should not be relied on.

questions.q: A 35-year-old driver is arrested for driving under the influence and refuses to take the blood, breath, or urine test. What is the penalty?
options: A 30-day suspension and no interlock device
A suspension of at least 45 days and an ignition interlock device for at least six months
A 90-day suspension and an ignition interlock device for at least six months
A suspension of at least 45 days and an ignition interlock device for at least one year
questions.ref: p.33 Alcohol and the Law: regardless of age, refusing a test means suspension of at least 45 days and an ignition interlock device for at least one year (failing the test for an adult carries an IID of at least six months).

questions.q: Which of the following contains about the same amount of alcohol as one regular 12-ounce beer?
options: An 8-ounce glass of wine
A 5-ounce glass of wine
3 ounces of 80-proof liquor
4 ounces of 80-proof liquor
questions.ref: p.33 Alcohol and You: an alcohol drink is 1.5 oz of 80-proof liquor, 12 oz of beer, or a 5 oz glass of wine.

questions.q: You find a parking space that is 15 feet from a fire hydrant and 20 feet from a stop sign. Can you legally park there?
options: No, because it is within 25 feet of the stop sign
No, because you must be 25 feet from a hydrant
Yes, because both distances are far enough
Yes, because only 10 feet is required from a stop sign
questions.ref: p.37 No-Parking Zones: do not park within 25 feet of a stop sign; within 10 feet of a fire hydrant.

questions.q: A tire suddenly blows out while you are driving. What should you do?
options: Brake hard to stop as quickly as possible, then pull onto the shoulder
Steer sharply toward the shoulder as soon as the tire goes, to get off the road quickly
Hold the wheel tightly, keep straight, ease off the gas and use the brakes lightly
Shift into neutral and coast to a stop in your lane of travel
questions.ref: p.39 Tire Blowout: hold the wheel tightly, keep going straight, slow gradually, take your foot off the gas and use the brakes lightly; do not stop on the road if possible.

questions.q: A small plaque showing a speed is mounted below a curve warning sign. According to the manual, what is it?
options: The minimum speed you must maintain through the curve, even in bad weather
An advisory speed plaque, showing the advisory speed for that condition
The speed limit for the whole roadway beyond the curve
The maximum speed for trucks and buses only
questions.ref: p.49 Advisory Speed Plaque: usually installed below another warning sign to indicate the advisory speed for a condition (see also p.50 Turns and Curves).

questions.q: A bicycle sharrow, two chevrons painted above a bicycle symbol, is on the pavement of your lane. What does it mean?
options: The lane is reserved for bicycles only and motor vehicles may not enter
Passing is prohibited in this lane because bicycles may be present
Parking is permitted in this lane for bicycles only
The lane is shared, so vehicles or bicycles may be in it
questions.ref: p.44 Other Markings: a bicycle sharrow, two chevrons above a bicycle symbol, indicates the lane is shared; vehicle or bicycle traffic may be in the lane and it is an additional warning to watch for bicycles.

questions.q: At a HAWK pedestrian signal you see a flashing red light. What must you do?
options: Stop, then proceed once pedestrians have cleared the crosswalk
Stop and wait until the signal turns solid yellow
Slow down and proceed with caution
Proceed, because the signal has been deactivated
questions.ref: p.45 HAWK Signals: flashing red means the signal is about to deactivate; drivers must stop but may proceed when pedestrians have cleared the crosswalk.

questions.q: A learner's permit applicant answers 19 of the 25 knowledge test questions correctly. What is the result?
options: Passes, because 18 correct is the minimum
Does not pass, because 20 correct answers are needed
Passes, because 19 of 25 is the requirement
Does not pass, because 23 correct answers are needed
questions.ref: p.5 The Knowledge Test: the test consists of 25 questions and you need 20 correct answers to pass.

questions.q: A first-time license applicant passes the road test and pays the license fee at the DMV office. What does the applicant receive?
options: The permanent license card, handed over at the counter on the same day
A temporary paper card, with the permanent card mailed within about 90 days of the test
A receipt only, with the learner's permit staying valid until the card arrives
A temporary paper card, with the permanent card mailed within 20 days
questions.ref: p.8 Pay for Your License: DMV mails the permanent license card; qualified applicants receive a temporary paper card at the office, and the permanent card arrives through the mail within 20 days.

questions.q: A 19-year-old who has never held a license in any state obtains a learner's permit today. Which statement is correct?
options: She must hold the permit 90 days before the road test and take an 8-hour course
She may take the road test after 30 days because she is over 18 and the course is optional
She must hold the permit 120 days before the road test and complete a 30-hour course
She must hold the permit 180 days before the road test, with no safe driving course needed
questions.ref: p.7 Applicants 18 Years of Age or Older: must hold a learner's permit at least 90 days before the road test, and first-time applicants must take an 8-hour course on safe driving practices.

questions.q: Which of the following is required of the parent or legal guardian of a 16-year-old who obtains a learner's permit?
options: Complete the full 30-hour classroom course alongside the teen at a driving school
Provide 8 hours of behind-the-wheel training with the teen before the road test
Complete two hours of instruction with the teen on teen driving laws and dangers
Take the knowledge test along with the teen and pass with 20 correct answers
questions.ref: p.6 Parent Training Requirements: a parent or guardian must complete two hours of instruction with the teen concerning laws governing drivers under age 18 and the dangers of teen driving.

questions.q: A child is 20 months old and weighs 33 pounds. Which restraint does Connecticut require?
options: A forward-facing seat with a 5-point harness
A booster seat
An adult seat belt
A rear-facing car seat
questions.ref: p.12 Child Safety Requirements: if age and weight fall in two categories, the more restrictive requirement applies (under age 2 means rear-facing seat, even if weight exceeds 30 pounds).

questions.q: A vehicle owner's insurance lapses and the insurance company reports the cancellation to the DMV. The owner ignores the DMV warning notice. What happens?
options: The driver's license is suspended for 45 days
The registration of the vehicle is suspended
The owner is fined $75 on the spot
The vehicle is impounded
questions.ref: p.13 Connecticut Insurance Laws: failure to respond to your warning notice will result in suspension of the registration.

questions.q: You notice a water bottle rolling around on the floor of your car. Why should you secure it before driving?
options: It could roll under the brake pedal and prevent you from stopping
It could cause a tire to lose pressure whenever the car goes over a bump
It will cause the car to pull to one side when you apply the brakes
It could damage the exhaust system and let gases leak into the passenger compartment
questions.ref: p.12 Loose Objects: make sure there are no objects on the floor that could roll under the brake pedal and prevent you from stopping the vehicle.

questions.q: Safer drivers look at least 12 seconds ahead of their vehicles. About how far is that on the highway?
options: One city block
Half a mile
About a quarter of a mile (four city blocks)
Two city blocks
questions.ref: p.14 Look Ahead: in the city 12 seconds is about one block; on the highway it is about four city blocks (a quarter of a mile).

questions.q: You are on a multi-lane highway and need to move across three lanes to the left. What is the safest approach?
options: Wait until all lanes are clear, then cross all three at once
Change one lane at a time, checking for traffic each time
Sound your horn and cross quickly
Cross two lanes together and the last one separately
questions.ref: p.23 Changing Lanes: take one lane at a time; it is very difficult to determine that all lanes are free and safe to cross at once.

questions.q: You are on an entrance ramp and there is no opening in the highway traffic yet. What should you do?
options: Speed up and force your way into the gap between the vehicles in the main lane
Drive to the end of the ramp and stop there until a large enough gap appears
Stop at the beginning of the ramp and wait until traffic on the highway clears
Slow down on the ramp so you have room to speed up before merging
questions.ref: p.20 Space to Enter: if you have to wait for space, slow down on the ramp so you have room to speed up; do not drive to the end of the ramp and stop.

questions.q: You are traveling at 55 mph and want to pass on a two-lane road. About how much clear distance do you need to pass safely, counting oncoming traffic?
options: About 400 feet
About 800 feet
Over 1,600 feet (about one-third of a mile)
About one-quarter mile
questions.ref: p.23 Rules of Passing: at 55 mph you travel over 800 feet in 10 seconds and so does an oncoming vehicle, so you need over 1600 feet (about one-third mile).

questions.q: You are driving through an intersection when you hear a siren behind you. You have already entered the intersection. What should you do?
options: Drive through the intersection, then pull over to the right and stop
Stop immediately where you are inside the intersection and wait for it to pass
Pull over to the left side of the road just beyond the intersection
Speed up and stay ahead of the emergency vehicle until you can pull over
questions.ref: p.37 Right-of-Way: if you are in an intersection, drive through the intersection before you pull over to the right and stop.

questions.q: A motorcycle approaching an intersection has its left turn signal flashing. You want to turn left across its path. What should you do?
options: Assume it is turning and go ahead
Wait until you see that it is actually beginning to turn
Honk your horn to warn the rider
Speed up to pass in front of it
questions.ref: p.18 Motorcycles: do not assume a motorcycle is turning; its signals may not self-cancel. Do not pull out in front of it until you see it actually beginning to turn.

questions.q: You approach three horseback riders on a public road. According to the manual, how must they ride?
options: Two abreast near the center line, so drivers coming from both directions can see them
Single file along the left edge of the road, facing oncoming traffic as pedestrians do
Single file near the right curb or road edge, or on a usable right shoulder
In the middle of the lane, with a rider at the back signaling for the group
questions.ref: p.18 Horses: horseback riders must ride single file near the right curb or road edge, or on a usable right shoulder, lane or path.

questions.q: You are driving on a four-lane divided highway with a grassy median. A school bus traveling toward you on the other roadway has its red lights flashing. What must you do?
options: Stop, because the bus has its red lights flashing, even though it is on the other roadway
Stop only if you can see children waiting at the side of the road
Slow to 10 mph and proceed past the bus once you have checked for children
You are not required to stop, because a median separates the roadways
questions.ref: p.37 Right-of-Way: you must stop for a school bus with red lights flashing, but you are not required to stop if the bus is traveling toward you and a median or other physical barrier separates the roadway.

questions.q: You are driving along a street with a bicycle lane on your right and plan to turn right at the next corner. What should you do?
options: Stay out of the bike lane until you turn, and yield to bicyclists before crossing it
Move into the bike lane well before the corner so you are in position to turn right
Drive in the bike lane with your hazard lights on so bicyclists can see you
Turn without yielding if your turn signal is on, since bicyclists must yield to cars
questions.ref: p.17 Bicyclists: do not drive in a bicycle lane when approaching a turn; you may turn across a bike lane but must yield to bicyclists in the lane before you turn across it.

questions.q: You normally drive 50 mph on this road when it is dry. The road is now covered with packed snow. About how fast should you drive?
options: 40 mph
25 mph
5 mph
45 mph
questions.ref: p.25 Slippery Roads: on packed snow you should cut your speed in half (on a wet road, reduce speed by about 10 mph).

questions.q: After a road dispute, a hostile motorist begins following you. What should you do?
options: Drive home as quickly as possible and lock the doors once you are inside
Pull over and make eye contact with the driver to try to calm him down peacefully
Stop on the shoulder and wait until the driver gives up and leaves
Do not go home; drive to a police station or other well-lit public place
questions.ref: p.26 Eye Contact: do not make eye contact; if a motorist pursues you, do not go home but drive to a police station, convenience store, or other public, well-lit location.

questions.q: A friend says that coffee and a cold shower will sober him up quickly before he drives. According to the manual:
options: Coffee works within about 30 minutes
Fresh air and exercise are enough
Nothing helps except time
A cold shower works if it lasts 15 minutes
questions.ref: p.33 Alcohol and You: there is no way to sober up quickly; coffee, fresh air, exercise, or cold showers will not help; time is the only thing.

questions.q: A 16-year-old driver is convicted of speeding 20 mph over the limit for the second time. What does DMV impose?
options: A 90-day suspension, a $175 license restoration fee, and court fines
A 60-day suspension, a $175 license restoration fee, and court fines
A 6-month suspension, a $175 license restoration fee, and court fines
A 30-day suspension, a $175 license restoration fee, and court fines
questions.ref: p.34 Other Suspensions table: speeding (20 mph over) is a 60-day suspension for a first offense, 90-day for a second offense, and 6-month for a third, with a $175 restoration fee and court fines.

questions.q: You reach an intersection with no stop sign, yield sign, or traffic signal. Another vehicle approaches at the same time from your right. Who must yield?
options: The vehicle on the right must yield, because you arrived first
The smaller vehicle must yield to the larger vehicle
The faster vehicle must yield to the slower vehicle
You must yield to the vehicle coming from the right
questions.ref: p.36 Right-of-Way: at an intersection with no stop sign, yield sign or signal, drivers must yield to vehicles coming from the right.

questions.q: Heavy fog limits your sight to about 200 feet. Which is about the fastest speed at which you can safely stop within what you can see?
options: 50 mph
30 mph
60 mph
70 mph
questions.ref: p.36 How Well Can You See: at 30 mph it takes about 200 feet to stop; if you cannot see 200 feet ahead you may not be driving safely at 30 mph (400 feet at 50 mph).

questions.q: An orange diamond-shaped sign with black symbols most likely warns of:
options: A hospital or other service nearby
A state route marker
Construction or maintenance work ahead
A railroad crossing ahead
questions.ref: p.47 Colors, p.51 Work Area Signs: orange signs alert you to possible dangers due to construction and maintenance projects.

questions.q: You are in the lane that has a solid yellow line on your side of the center, with a dashed yellow line on the other side. May you pass another vehicle?
options: No, passing is not permitted on the side of the solid line
Yes, passing is permitted in either direction
Yes, if no oncoming vehicle is visible
No, passing is never permitted on a two-lane road
questions.ref: p.44 Center Lines: a dashed yellow line alongside a solid yellow line indicates passing is permitted on the side of the broken line, but not on the side of the solid line.

questions.q: A white X-shaped 'crossbuck' sign at a railroad crossing has the same meaning as which sign?
options: Stop sign
Do Not Enter sign
Merge sign
Yield sign
questions.ref: p.52 Railroad Crossbuck: this sign has the same meaning as a Yield sign; you must yield to crossing trains.

questions.q: The 19-year-old brother of a 17-year-old applicant, who has held a license for five years, offers to do the home training. Can he serve as the home instructor?
options: Yes, because he has held a license for more than four years
Yes, because he lives in the same household
Yes, if a parent rides along
No, because a home instructor must be at least 20 years old
questions.ref: p.6 Home Training Program: the instructor must be at least 20 years of age and have held a license for four or more years without suspension.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a restriction on 16- and 17-year-old licensed drivers?
options: Operating a vanpool vehicle
Driving on interstate highways
Transporting more passengers than there are seat belts
Using a hands-free cell phone while driving
questions.ref: p.8 Other Restrictions: teens may not transport more passengers than seat belts, operate a vehicle requiring a public passenger permit or a vanpool vehicle, or use a cell phone even hands-free; highways are not restricted.

questions.q: A 16-year-old with a learner's permit plans to take the road test in a rented car. According to the manual:
options: This is allowed if the rental agreement lists the teen as an additional authorized driver
This is allowed with a parent's signature on the rental contract and the permit
Not allowed, since without a valid license you cannot test in a rented vehicle
This is allowed only for the Class D road test and not for other classes
questions.ref: p.7 The Road Test: if you do not have a valid driver's license you cannot test in a rented vehicle; the vehicle must be mechanically safe with valid registration and proof of insurance.

questions.q: Your driver's license says you must wear corrective lenses, and you are stopped by a law enforcement officer without them. What may happen?
options: You may be issued a citation
You will receive only a verbal warning
Nothing, if it is daytime
Your license will be suspended for 45 days
questions.ref: p.5 The Vision Test: if your license says you must wear corrective lenses and you are stopped while not wearing them, you may be issued a citation.

questions.q: Which of the following is a legal use of a hand-held phone by an adult driver?
options: Texting a reply while stopped at a red light
Calling an emergency response operator to report an emergency
Reading a message while stopped in a traffic jam
Dialing a friend while stopped at a stop sign
questions.ref: p.13 Cell Phone Laws: hand-held devices are prohibited even when temporarily stopped for traffic or a signal; the exceptions include an emergency situation contacting an emergency response operator.

questions.q: A driver says he does not need to wear a seat belt because his car has airbags. Why is he wrong?
options: Airbags are designed to work only in low-speed city driving, so belts matter on highways
Belts are required only for passengers in the rear seat, because the airbag protects the driver
Airbags protect against every kind of crash, but officers rarely check for belts
The law requires belts, and airbags do not protect you in side or rear crashes or rollovers
questions.ref: p.12 Seat Belt Laws: state law requires safety belts even if the vehicle has airbags; airbags do not protect you if hit from the side or rear or if the vehicle rolls over.

questions.q: When you apply your brakes, your vehicle pulls to one side. What should you do?
options: Have the braking system serviced
Ignore it if the brakes still stop the vehicle
Replace the windshield wipers
Have the headlights aimed
questions.ref: p.11 Braking System: if the vehicle pulls to one side when the brake is applied, this indicates a problem in the braking system and it should be serviced.

questions.q: At a railroad crossing with two tracks, a train has just passed. What should you do before crossing?
options: Cross immediately, since the only train that was coming has now passed
Cross as fast as possible to spend the least time on the second set of tracks
Wait until the train is well down the track, since it may hide another train
Honk your horn to warn any other train that you are about to cross the tracks
questions.ref: p.15 Railroad Crossings: at crossings with more than one track, wait until the passing train is well down the track; the train that just passed may hide another one.

questions.q: Lane markings at an intersection allow two lanes to turn right. You are in the left of the two turning lanes. What should you do during the turn?
options: Drift into the right-hand turning lane to finish closer to the curb
Cut across the other turning lane so you end up in the lane nearest the one you came from
Slow to a stop in the middle of the turn to let the other lane go first
Stay in your lane for the whole turn
questions.ref: p.24 Multiple lanes turning: if signs or lane markings allow two or more turning lanes, stay in your lane during the turn.

questions.q: You are descending a long, steep hill. What should you do regarding traffic behind you?
options: Keep your eyes forward on the road and ignore your mirrors until you reach the bottom
Check your mirrors, since large trucks and buses often build up speed going downhill
Speed up on the downgrade to stay ahead of the heavy vehicles behind you
Move to the left lane, since heavy vehicles are required to stay in the right lane
questions.ref: p.24 Hills and Curves: check your mirrors going down hills; vehicles often build up speed, so be alert for large trucks and buses that may be going too fast.

questions.q: You are driving alongside, but slightly behind, another vehicle on a multi-lane road. What should you do?
options: Speed up or drop back so the other driver can see you
Stay where you are to keep pace with traffic
Sound your horn to alert the driver
Flash your high beams
questions.ref: p.22 Blind Spots: avoid driving on either side and slightly to the rear of another vehicle; speed up or drop back so the other driver can see your vehicle.

questions.q: A tractor-trailer is approaching an intersection ahead in the right lane. You are behind it, and the right side looks clear. What should you NOT do?
options: Stay well back and let the truck complete its turn before you proceed
Keep a safe following distance of at least three seconds so you can see around the truck
Pass on the right, because the truck could turn right and trap you against the curb
Wait until the truck has cleared the intersection before you go through
questions.ref: p.20 Trucks Make Wide Right Turns: resist the temptation to pass on the right of a truck approaching an intersection; if it turns right you could be caught between the truck and the curb.

questions.q: A blind pedestrian with a guide dog is crossing at a regulated intersection and your light turns green. What must you do?
options: Proceed, since you have the green light and the right-of-way over pedestrians
Sound your horn so the pedestrian will hurry across and clear your path
Proceed slowly past the pedestrian, leaving as much room as you can on the left
Stay stopped until the pedestrian is out of the road, despite your green light
questions.ref: p.16 White Canes and Guide Dogs: at regulated intersections, remain stopped until the pedestrian is out of the road, even if you have a green light. Also p.36: do not use your horn.

questions.q: A vehicle is pulled over on the shoulder of a two-lane road. What does Connecticut's Move Over Law require of you?
options: Slow down below the posted speed limit and move over one lane whenever it is safe
Stop behind the vehicle and offer help
Maintain your speed and sound your horn
Move over only if the vehicle is a police car
questions.ref: p.16 Move Over Law: when any vehicle is pulled over on any part of a highway or road, slow down (below the posted speed limit) and move over one lane whenever it is safe to do so.

questions.q: It is Saturday afternoon and you pass a sign warning of a school zone. School is closed. What is the correct approach?
options: Ignore the sign and keep your normal speed, since school is closed and no children should be around
Stay alert and obey the slower speed, since children are present outside school hours too
Speed up to clear the school area quickly, since no crossing guards are on duty on weekends
Stop completely at the sign and wait for a crossing guard to wave you on
questions.ref: p.16 Children at Play and School Zones: school hours are not the only time children are present; you must obey the slower posted speed limit in school zones.

questions.q: A farm tractor with an orange triangle decal is traveling 20 mph ahead of you in a no-passing zone marked with double yellow lines. According to the manual, you:
options: May never pass, because a double yellow line prohibits passing in either direction
May pass only by driving on the right shoulder, if it is paved
May pass if you can see far enough ahead to complete the pass safely
May pass only if the tractor stops and signals you to go around
questions.ref: p.18 Slow Moving Vehicles: state law permits passing slow moving vehicles in no-passing zones; you may cross a double yellow line but must be able to see far enough ahead to pass safely.

questions.q: You are approaching a sharp curve at a speed that feels too fast. What should you do?
options: Slow down before you enter the curve so you do not have to brake in it
Brake hard once you are in the curve
Accelerate to pull through the curve
Shift into neutral and coast through
questions.ref: p.25 Curves: always slow down before you enter the curve; braking in a curve can cause the vehicle to skid.

questions.q: The car ahead of you drifts over the lane lines and the driver is busy with food. What should you do?
options: Pass immediately, before the driver drifts into your lane
Honk repeatedly to get the driver's attention back on the road
Tailgate closely to stay in the driver's view so he or she sees you
Give the driver plenty of room and follow at 3 to 4 seconds
questions.ref: p.27 Driver Distractions: give a distracted driver plenty of room and maintain a safe following distance of 3 to 4 seconds; be careful when passing.

questions.q: A 20-year-old is arrested for DUI on private property and tests at .02 percent. How does zero tolerance apply?
options: It applies only on public roads and does not reach private property, so no penalty applies
It applies on public roads and private property, so the driver faces penalties
It applies only to drivers under 18, so a 20-year-old would not be penalized
It applies only if the driver was involved in a crash, so no penalty applies
questions.ref: p.33 Alcohol and the Law: if under 21 you are subject to zero tolerance, with penalties for any measurable amount of alcohol, .02% or more, on both public roads and private property.

questions.q: You took an allergy medicine and are not sure whether it is safe to drive. What should you do?
options: Drive carefully, since over-the-counter drugs are always safe before driving
Drink a couple of cups of coffee to counteract any drowsiness before you drive
Check the label, and ask your doctor or pharmacist if you are unsure
Take only half the dose so it will not affect your driving
questions.ref: p.33 Drugs and Driving: drugs for allergies or colds can make a person drowsy; check the label for warnings and ask your doctor or pharmacist if unsure.

questions.q: You are in a roundabout, and a driver at one of the entries is waiting to enter. What should you do?
options: Stop within the roundabout to let the waiting driver enter ahead of you
Slow to a stop in your lane and wave the waiting driver in
Yield to the entering driver, since he arrived at the intersection first
Continue through the roundabout; do not stop in it to let others enter
questions.ref: p.37 Roundabouts: entering traffic must yield to circulating traffic; do not stop within the roundabout to allow traffic to enter from another leg.

questions.q: Which statement about making a U-turn is correct?
options: Signal left, stop, check traffic, then move into the outside or right-hand lane going the other way
U-turns are legal on any road unless a sign specifically prohibits them, even on expressways
Give a left turn signal, stop, check traffic, then proceed into the left lane going the opposite way
No signal is needed once you have stopped, because other drivers can see you turning around
questions.ref: p.37 U-Turns: check for signs prohibiting them; never on an expressway; give a left signal, stop, check traffic, and proceed into the outside or right-hand lane in the opposite direction.

questions.q: You see a round yellow sign with an 'X' and the letters 'RR' beside the road. What should you do?
options: Yield to traffic on the cross street
Slow down, look and listen, because a railroad crossing is ahead
Prepare to merge
Reduce speed because a school zone is ahead
questions.ref: p.46, p.52: a circular sign indicates that you are approaching a railroad crossing; slow down, look and listen for trains.

questions.q: A reversible lane has overhead signals. You see a steady yellow 'X' over your lane. What does it mean?
options: The lane is for turning only, so you may use it only to make a turn
You cannot use the lane, so you must stop until the signal changes
The lane's use is changing; move out of it as soon as it is safe
You may use the lane in either direction until the signal changes to green
questions.ref: p.44 Reversible Lanes: a steady yellow X means the use of the lane is changing and you should move out of it as soon as it is safe; flashing yellow X is for turning only; red X means you cannot use the lane.

questions.q: You approach an intersection where the traffic light is flashing red. What must you do?
options: Slow down and proceed with caution
Stop only if other traffic is present
Yield to crossing traffic
Come to a full stop, then proceed when it is safe, as at a stop sign
questions.ref: p.45 Flashing Lights: a flashing red light means the same as a stop sign; you must come to a full stop and may proceed when it is safe.

questions.q: During the first six months after a 16-year-old receives a license, which passenger is allowed?
options: His parent, who holds a valid driver's license
His 18-year-old sister, who has held a license for two years
A 19-year-old friend who has held a license for three years
Two classmates, as long as each has a seat belt
questions.ref: p.8 Passenger Restrictions: in the first six months only a licensed instructor, parents/guardian (at least one with a valid license), or one person at least 20 who held a license four or more consecutive years.

questions.q: A 17-year-old is convicted of using a cell phone while driving for the first time. What does DMV impose?
options: A warning only
A 60-day suspension
A 30-day suspension and a $175 license restoration fee
A 6-month suspension
questions.ref: p.34 Other Suspensions table: use of cell phone or text messaging is a 30-day suspension on a first offense, $175 restoration fee, court fines (90 days second, 6 months third).

questions.q: Connecticut law requires a minimum number of supervised behind-the-wheel hours before licensing. What are the required and the recommended amounts?
options: 30 hours required, 40 hours recommended
40 hours required, 100 hours recommended
8 hours required, 40 hours recommended
100 hours required, 200 hours recommended
questions.ref: p.30 Tips for Supervising Adults: law requires a minimum of 40 hours of supervised driving; at least 100 hours is recommended.

questions.q: Where must the person giving instruction to a learner's permit holder sit?
options: In the back seat, where he or she can watch the learner's mirrors
In any seat that has a seat belt, as long as the instructor is alert
In another vehicle following closely behind the learner's car
In the front passenger seat, alert and ready to take over
questions.ref: p.5 Qualified Trainer Requirement: the instructor must sit in the front passenger seat next to the learner and be alert and ready to take over control of the vehicle.

questions.q: A parent wants to put a rear-facing infant seat in the front passenger seat of a car that has a functional passenger-side airbag. What does the law say?
options: It is allowed if the child is under 2
It is allowed if the seat has a 5-point harness
The law prohibits it
It is allowed if the airbag is switched to the lowest setting
questions.ref: p.12 Child Safety Requirements: the law prohibits the placement of a rear-facing child restraint system in the front seat of a vehicle with a functional passenger-side airbag.

questions.q: A driver says seat belts are only needed on long trips and not for driving around town. According to the manual:
options: Over half of traffic deaths happen within 25 miles of home, many on roads under 45 mph
Most traffic deaths occur on interstates and other highways far from the driver's home
Belts are not required on local roads posted under 45 mph, only on faster highways
Short trips close to home are statistically much safer, so belts matter less
questions.ref: p.13 Misconceptions: over half of all traffic deaths happen within 25 miles of home, many on roads posted at less than 45 mph.

questions.q: Other drivers often flash their headlights at you at night. What should you do?
options: Turn on your high beams so the other drivers can see you better
Ignore it, since flashing headlights only mean other drivers are being friendly or courteous
Switch to your parking lights so you stop blinding other drivers
Have a mechanic check them, since an out-of-line headlight can blind other drivers
questions.ref: p.11 Lights: an out-of-line headlight may blind other drivers; if other drivers often flash their headlights at you, have a mechanic check the headlights.

questions.q: You are pulling a trailer. Which following distance does the manual suggest?
options: Two seconds, since you are slower
Four seconds, because the extra weight increases your stopping distance
One second per 10 mph
Three seconds is always enough
questions.ref: p.21 When to use the four-second rule: pulling a trailer, the extra weight increases your stopping distance.

questions.q: You want to cross a four-lane road with a narrow median. Part of your vehicle would stick out into traffic if you stopped there. What should you do?
options: Wait until you can cross the entire road without stopping in the median
Stop in the median anyway
Cross as quickly as you can without looking
Use your horn to warn traffic
questions.ref: p.21 Space to Cross: stopping halfway across traffic is only safe when the median divider is large enough for your vehicle; do not stop in a divider where part of your vehicle sticks into traffic.

questions.q: When is it safe to return to your lane after passing another vehicle?
options: As soon as the front of your car has moved past the rear of the other vehicle
When you have signaled for at least two full seconds, whatever the gap
When you can see both of its headlights in your rear-view mirror
When the vehicle you passed slows down or flashes its lights
questions.ref: p.23 Return to your lane: when you can see both headlights of the vehicle you just passed in your rear-view mirror, it is safe to return.

questions.q: You are backing out of a parking space. Which is the correct technique?
options: Rely on your rearview mirror alone and back quickly to clear the space
Rely on your side mirrors only, since they show both sides of the car
Back with your eyes on the door mirror and flash your lights to warn others
Look over your right shoulder through the rear window and back slowly
questions.ref: p.24 Backing: turn around and look over your right shoulder so you can look directly through the rear window; do not depend on mirrors; back slowly.

questions.q: You are parked on the street and about to get out of your vehicle on the traffic side. What should you do first?
options: Open the door quickly and get out before any traffic reaches the back of your car
Check the sides and rear for bicyclists and traffic before opening the door
Sound your horn to warn traffic and bicyclists that you are getting out
Turn on your headlights so approaching traffic and bicyclists see your car
questions.ref: p.16, p.17: do not open a vehicle door if it hits or gets in the way of a pedestrian, bicyclist or traffic; check to the sides and rear for bicyclists before you open your door.

questions.q: A bicyclist is riding in the center of a narrow lane ahead of you. What should you do?
options: Be patient; pass only when you can give at least three feet of space
Honk twice to tell the bicyclist to move over so you can pass without delay
Squeeze past quickly, leaving about one foot of space between you and the bicyclist
Pass on the shoulder, where the bicyclist cannot reach you
questions.ref: p.17 Bicyclists: a bicyclist may take the travel lane when the lane is too narrow; pass only when you can give a minimum of three feet; do not sound your horn.

questions.q: You are driving at night and an oncoming motorcycle approaches. Why does the manual tell you to dim your headlights?
options: High beams wash out a motorcycle's turn signals, which may not cancel by themselves anyway
Dimming is required only when the motorcycle is carrying a passenger or a heavy load
Motorcycles do not have a low beam, so oncoming drivers must dim to compensate
High beams can blind a vulnerable motorcyclist far more dangerously than other drivers
questions.ref: p.18 Motorcycles: always dim your headlights when approaching a motorcycle; because of their vulnerability the blinding effect of high beams can be far more dangerous to them than to drivers of motor vehicles.

questions.q: You are driving beside a large truck and cannot see the driver's face in the truck's side mirror. What does that mean?
options: The driver can still see you in the other side mirror, so you may stay
The driver is looking away from the mirror and will check it shortly
He cannot see you, so speed up or drop back out of the No-Zone
You are in a safe position as long as you match the truck's speed
questions.ref: p.19 Side No-Zones: if you can't see the driver's face in his side view mirror, he can't see you; never stay alongside a large vehicle (p.22).

questions.q: A pedestrian waiting at the entrance to a crosswalk moves the front wheels of a stroller into the crosswalk. What must you do?
options: Continue, since the pedestrian has not stepped off the curb
Slow or stop and grant the right-of-way
Wait only if there is a traffic signal
Sound your horn
questions.ref: p.16 Pedestrians: a pedestrian indicates intent to cross by moving into the crosswalk's entrance any extension of a body part, including a stroller; drivers must slow or stop and grant the right-of-way.

questions.q: Why can a bridge be icy when the road leading to it is not?
options: Bridges are made of metal, which collects ice faster than any other road surface
Salt trucks are not allowed to spread salt on bridges, so ice builds up there
Bridges are always shaded by trees and buildings, so the sun never reaches them
Bridges have no earth beneath to insulate them, so they get colder and icier
questions.ref: p.25 Slippery Roads: pavement on bridges can be icy even when other pavement is not because bridges do not have earth underneath to insulate them.

questions.q: Your tires run over a shoulder rumble strip. What should you do?
options: Pull off the road at a safe place immediately and check your alertness level
Return to the lane and continue
Turn up the radio
Speed up to reach your destination
questions.ref: p.28 Fatigue: if you run over a shoulder rumble strip, pull off the road at a safe place immediately and check your alertness level.

questions.q: A newly licensed 17-year-old says alcohol affects him no more than it affects an experienced adult driver. According to the manual, what is wrong with that claim?
options: Alcohol affects only drivers who have held a license for less than six months
Alcohol affects drivers only after the third drink, so the claim is true for one drink
New drivers are more affected by alcohol because they are still learning to drive
Alcohol affects only drivers under 18, because of Connecticut's zero tolerance law
questions.ref: p.33 Drinking and Driving: no one can drink alcohol and drive safely; new drivers are more affected by alcohol than experienced drivers because they are still learning to drive.

questions.q: A 16-year-old is convicted of reckless driving for the first time. What penalty does DMV impose?
options: A 30-day suspension, a $175 restoration fee, and court fines or up to 30 days in prison
A 6-month suspension, a $175 restoration fee, and court fines or up to 30 days in prison
A 60-day suspension, a $175 restoration fee, and court fines or up to 30 days in prison
A 1-year suspension, a $175 restoration fee, and court fines or up to one year in prison
questions.ref: p.34 Other Suspensions table: reckless driving first offense is a 6-month suspension, $175 restoration fee, court fines or imprisonment of not more than 30 days, or both.

questions.q: It is a rainy afternoon, and you turn on your windshield wipers. What else does the law require?
options: Turn on your headlights
Turn on your high beams
Turn on your parking lights
Turn on your hazard flashers
questions.ref: p.38 Use Headlights: if you turn on your wipers, turn on your headlights. It's the law.

questions.q: You approach a crash scene where police and an ambulance have already arrived, and you were not involved. What should you do?
options: Stop and offer help to the injured people at the scene
Slow to a crawl so you can see what happened and whether anyone needs help
Pull over and watch from the shoulder until the road is clear
Keep moving, watching for people in or near the road
questions.ref: p.41 Traffic Crashes: do not stop at an accident unless you are involved or emergency help has not yet arrived; keep moving.

questions.q: A diamond-shaped yellow warning sign shows two lanes becoming one. What does it mean?
options: Do not pass
The road ends
Drivers in both lanes are responsible for merging smoothly
The left lane is exit only
questions.ref: p.49 Merge: two lanes of traffic are about to become one; drivers in both lanes are responsible for merging smoothly.

questions.q: Flashing lights and lowered gates warn that a train is approaching a crossing. Which statement about pedestrians is correct?
options: Pedestrians may cross if they can see no train, since only vehicles must stop
Pedestrians may not cross when a signal, gate, flagman or officer warns of a train
Pedestrians may duck under a lowered gate, as long as they cross the tracks quickly
Pedestrians may cross while the lights flash as long as the gates are still up
questions.ref: p.52 Railroad Crossing, Flashing Lights and Gate: pedestrians may not cross railroad tracks when warned of a train by an automatic signal, crossing gates, flagman or law enforcement officer.

questions.q: A lane has a white diamond painted on the pavement and a sign with the letters HOV. Which vehicles may use it?
options: Vehicles carrying more than one person, with signs posted telling how many people must be in the vehicle
Buses only, as in a lane marked "transit"
Bicycles only, as in a lane marked "bicycle"
Emergency vehicles only, at any time of day
questions.ref: p.44 Reserved Lanes: HOV stands for High Occupancy Vehicles; a diamond-shaped marker indicates lanes reserved for vehicles with more than one person, and signs say how many people must be in the vehicle.

questions.q: A 17-year-old learner's permit holder is practicing, and the trip is not a lesson with a commercial driving school instructor. Which passenger arrangement is permitted?
options: One licensed friend, age 18, who has held a license for over a year and is helping the teen practice
One person giving instruction who is at least 20 years old and has held a license for four or more consecutive years, with no suspension in the prior four years
Two licensed adults, age 21, who have each held a license for two years without any suspension
One adult, age 20, who has held a license for two years, plus the teen's licensed older brother
questions.ref: p.5-6 Permit passenger restrictions: only a licensed instructor (and those accompanying), or one person giving instruction who is 20+, licensed 4+ consecutive years, license not suspended in prior four years.

questions.q: A 16-year-old receives a learner's permit on March 1 and completes the full driver education program through a licensed commercial driving school. What is the earliest the road test may be taken?
options: 60 days after the permit was issued
90 days after the permit was issued
180 days after the permit was issued
120 days after the permit was issued
questions.ref: p.6 Applicants who complete driver ed through a commercial driving school or secondary school must wait 120 days after permit issuance; all others 180 days.

questions.q: A 16-year-old who has held a license for eight months is driving at 11:45 p.m. Which trip would still violate the curfew restriction?
options: Driving home from a friend's house after watching a movie
Driving home from a late shift at a part-time job
Driving to a late-night religious service
Driving as the assigned driver in the Safe Ride Program
questions.ref: p.8 Hour restriction 11 p.m.-5 a.m. unless traveling for employment, school, religious activities, medical necessity, or as an assigned Safe Ride driver; visiting friends is not an exception.

questions.q: A 17-year-old is convicted for the first time of driving 20 mph over the speed limit. What does the DMV impose?
options: A 30-day suspension and a $175 license restoration fee
A 90-day suspension and a $175 license restoration fee
A 60-day suspension and a $175 license restoration fee
A 6-month suspension and a $175 license restoration fee
questions.ref: p.34 Suspension table: Speeding (20 mph over) 1st offense = 60-day suspension; 2nd = 90-day; 3rd = 6-month.

questions.q: You are driving a neighbor's 12-year-old to a soccer game, and the child unbuckles the seat belt during the ride. What is your obligation as the driver?
options: You must make sure that any passenger between 7 and 16 years old is wearing a safety belt, and both of you could be cited if the child is not
Only the child's parents can be cited, because a driver is responsible only for passengers who are younger than 7 years old and who ride in a child restraint
None, because a child who is age 8 or older and weighs 60 pounds or more may choose between a booster seat and no restraint
You must buckle only the passengers under age 7, since passengers between 7 and 16 years old are responsible for themselves
questions.ref: p.13 Seat belts: ALL drivers are obligated to ensure any passenger between 7 and 16 years old wears a seat safety belt; if the driver or passenger fails to wear one, each could be cited.

questions.q: You are 25 years old and your car is stopped in a traffic jam on a public highway. Which action is legal?
options: Holding your phone to talk, because your vehicle is not moving
Typing a text message while the car is stopped
Holding your phone to read navigation directions since traffic has stopped you
Talking on the phone through a hands-free accessory
questions.ref: p.13 Hand-held devices are prohibited even when temporarily stopped by traffic; only hands-free accessories are permitted.

questions.q: You do the penny test on a tire, placing Lincoln's head into the groove where the tread looks lowest. Which result shows a safe amount of tread?
options: All of Lincoln's head is visible above the tread
The tread reaches only the edge of the penny and does not touch the head
Some part of Lincoln's head is covered by the tread
Lincoln's head is fully visible but the tire is at the recommended psi
questions.ref: p.11 Penny test: if any part of Lincoln's head is covered by the tread you have the safe amount of tread.

questions.q: On the highway, safer drivers look at least 12 seconds ahead. About how far is that distance?
options: About one city block
About four city blocks, or a quarter of a mile
About one-third of a mile
About half a mile
questions.ref: p.14 On the highway 12 seconds is about four city blocks (a quarter of a mile); in the city it is about one block.

questions.q: You want to parallel park on a busy street, and a line of traffic is coming up behind you. What does the manual say to do?
options: Stop in the travel lane with your hazard flashers on and back into the space quickly so you hold up the traffic as little as possible
Put on your turn signal, pull up next to the space, and allow the following vehicles to pass before you park
Slow down quickly and brake hard so that the vehicles behind you learn to go around you before you start to park
Drive past the space and park in the next legal spot ahead, because stopping alongside a space is never permitted with traffic behind you
questions.ref: p.22 Space Behind: when you want to parallel park and traffic is coming behind you, put on your turn signal, pull next to the space and allow following vehicles to pass before you park.

questions.q: You are on a highway and realize you just missed your exit. What does the manual say to do?
options: Back up slowly along the shoulder until you reach the exit
Stop in the travel lane with flashers on and back up to the exit
Continue on to where you can safely turn around
Slow suddenly and cross several lanes to reach the next ramp
questions.ref: p.24 Backing: if you miss your turn or exit, do not back up but go on to where you can safely turn around.

questions.q: You are traveling at 55 mph on a two-lane road and want to pass. What does the manual say you need in oncoming traffic?
options: About a 4-second opening, or about 400 feet
About a 10-second opening, or about 800 feet
About a 5-second opening, or about 1,600 feet
About a 10-second opening, or over 1,600 feet
questions.ref: p.23 At 55 mph you need about 10 seconds to pass; you travel over 800 feet and so does the oncoming vehicle, so you need over 1,600 feet (about one-third mile).

questions.q: You are driving on a divided highway where a concrete barrier separates the two directions. A school bus on the other side, traveling toward you, has its red lights flashing. What must you do?
options: Stop, because you must stop for a school bus on the opposite side of the road
You are not required to stop, because a physical barrier separates the roadway
Slow to 5 mph and pass the bus carefully
Stop only if you can see children on your side of the road
questions.ref: p.37 Must stop for a school bus with red lights flashing on either side, but not required if the bus is traveling toward you and a median or physical barrier separates the roadway.

questions.q: You are following a tractor-trailer on a dark highway at night and want to see farther ahead. What does the manual say about your high beams?
options: Never use them while following a truck at night, because the glare in the truck's large side mirrors can blind the truck driver
Use them freely, because a truck driver sits too high above the road to be bothered by the lights of a car behind the trailer
Use them only if you drift into the truck's rear No-Zone, so that the driver can see that your car is there behind the trailer
Use them only on unlit roads, since low beams reflect back off the trailer's rear doors and reduce how far you can see ahead
questions.ref: p.20 Keep a Safe Following Distance Behind Trucks: never use your high beams when following a truck at night; the glare in the large side mirrors can blind the truck driver.

questions.q: A vehicle is pulled over on the side of the road ahead of you on a multi-lane highway. What does the Move Over Law require?
options: Slow down below the posted speed limit and move over one lane when it is safe to do so
Come to a complete stop until the vehicle drives away
Keep your speed and lane, because the vehicle is already off the travel lanes
Move over only if the stopped vehicle is a police or emergency vehicle
questions.ref: p.16 Move Over Law: when any vehicle is pulled over on any part of a highway, SLOW DOWN (below posted limit) and move over one lane whenever safe.

questions.q: A truck's blind spots can stretch about how far in front of the cab and behind the truck?
options: About 10 feet in front of the cab and about 100 feet behind the truck
About 200 feet in front of the cab and about 20 feet behind the truck
About 65 feet in front of the cab and about 400 feet behind the truck
About 20 feet in front of the cab and about 200 feet behind the truck
questions.ref: p.19 Wide Turns: blind spots may stretch up to 20 feet in front of the cab and approximately 200 feet behind the truck.

questions.q: You are about to turn right at the next intersection and see a bicyclist ahead of you traveling in the same direction. What should you do?
options: Pass the bicyclist quickly, then turn right immediately
Slow down and let the bicyclist clear the intersection before you make your turn
Speed up and turn before the bicyclist reaches the intersection
Sound your horn so the bicyclist moves out of your way, then turn
questions.ref: p.17 Do not pass a bicyclist immediately before a right turn; slow down and let the cyclist clear the intersection; also avoid horn near bicyclists.

questions.q: The posted limit is 40 mph and the road is covered with packed snow. According to the manual, about how fast should you drive?
options: About 20 mph
About 30 mph
About 35 mph
At a crawl, under 5 mph
questions.ref: p.25 On a wet road reduce speed about 10 mph; on packed snow cut speed in half; on ice slow to a crawl.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the things the manual says to do before a long trip to avoid a fatigue-related crash?
options: Get adequate sleep, since most adults need 7 to 9 hours to maintain proper alertness during the day, and avoid starting a trip when tired
Wait to stop for a break until you have driven about 300 miles or 5 hours, so that you make better time on the trip
Arrange for a travel companion, someone to talk with and to share the driving during the trip
Avoid alcohol and sedating medications, checking your labels or asking your doctor about them
questions.ref: p.28 Before a Trip: get 7 to 9 hours of sleep, schedule breaks about every 100 miles or 2 hours, arrange a travel companion, avoid alcohol and sedating medications; waiting 300 miles or 5 hours is not listed.

questions.q: A 19-year-old driver is arrested for DUI and the test result is .02 percent. What are the minimum consequences?
options: License suspended for at least 45 days, and an ignition interlock device for at least six months
License suspended for at least 30 days, and an ignition interlock device for at least one year
License suspended for at least 45 days, and an ignition interlock device for at least one year
License suspended for at least 90 days, and an ignition interlock device for at least six months
questions.ref: p.33 Under 21 zero tolerance (.02% or more): suspension at least 45 days and IID at least one year as condition of reinstatement.

questions.q: You and two friends are planning an evening where alcohol will be served. Which plan does the manual recommend to avoid drinking and driving?
options: Agree that whoever has had the fewest drinks will drive, and let that driver sober up with coffee and fresh air before leaving
Switch from liquor to beer or wine, since the manual says a driver is not impaired by drinks that have less alcohol in them
Go together and agree which one of you will not drink alcohol, rotating among the group as the designated driver
Let the youngest driver have one regular drink with dinner, since new drivers are affected less than experienced drivers
questions.ref: p.33 Alcohol and You: arrange to go with two or more persons and agree which one will not drink; rotate as a designated driver, or use public transportation or a cab.

questions.q: Which parking spot is legal under the manual's no-parking rules?
options: Parking 20 feet from a stop sign
Parking 15 feet from a pedestrian safety zone
Parking about 18 inches from the curb
Parking 12 feet from a fire hydrant
questions.ref: p.37 Do not park within 25 ft of a stop sign or pedestrian safety zone, within 10 ft of a hydrant, or more than one foot from the curb.

questions.q: Visibility is poor and you can see only about 250 feet ahead on dry pavement with good tires and brakes. Using the manual's stopping figures, which statement is correct?
options: 50 mph is too fast, because stopping from that speed takes about 400 feet
30 mph is too fast, because stopping from that speed takes about 400 feet
30 mph is too fast, because stopping from that speed takes about 200 feet
Neither speed is too fast, because stopping on dry pavement always takes less than 250 feet
questions.ref: p.36 At 50 mph it takes about 400 feet to stop; at 30 mph about 200 feet. If you cannot see 400 feet ahead you may not be safe at 50 mph.

questions.q: You are driving on a two-lane road. The center line has a solid yellow line on your side and a dashed yellow line on the oncoming traffic's side. You want to pass a car traveling at the speed limit. Passing is:
options: Permitted for you whenever no oncoming vehicle is in sight
Permitted for you and for oncoming drivers, because one line is dashed
Not permitted for you, although oncoming drivers may pass
Not permitted for either direction until the lines change
questions.ref: p.44 A dashed yellow line alongside a solid yellow line means passing is permitted on the side of the broken line, but not on the side of the solid line.

questions.q: You approach a work zone where a flagger is directing traffic through the area. Which statement is correct according to the manual?
options: Flaggers normally wear orange or yellow vests or yellow-green shirts or jackets and use STOP/SLOW paddles and red flags, and you must obey them
Flaggers use only hand signals, so a STOP/SLOW paddle or a red flag need not be obeyed unless a police officer is also present at the work zone
Flaggers wear ordinary street clothes, so you should follow only the directions given by a uniformed police officer
Flaggers are posted only when workers are visible, so you may ignore the Flag Person sign if you cannot see any workers
questions.ref: p.51 Work Area Signs/Flag Person: flaggers normally wear orange or yellow vests or yellow-green shirts or jackets, use STOP/SLOW paddles and red flags, and drivers must follow their directions.

questions.q: At a pedestrian crossing, a HAWK signal is showing solid yellow. What does this mean for drivers?
options: A pedestrian has just activated the signal, so proceed with caution
The signal has not been activated, so vehicles may proceed
The signal is about to deactivate; stop, but go when pedestrians clear
The pedestrian signal is about to change, and a red signal will be displayed next
questions.ref: p.45 HAWK: Solid Yellow - pedestrian signal about to change; motorists notified movement is ending and a red signal will be displayed.

questions.q: A 19-year-old who has never held a license in any state applies for a Connecticut license. Which combination of requirements applies?
options: Hold a learner's permit for at least 120 days and show proof of attending an 8-hour safe driving practices course
Hold a learner's permit for at least 90 days; the 8-hour course is required only for 16- and 17-year-olds
Hold a learner's permit for at least 90 days and show proof of attending an 8-hour safe driving practices course
Hold a learner's permit for at least 180 days and complete 40 hours of behind-the-wheel training
questions.ref: p.7 Applicants 18+ must hold a permit at least 90 days before the road test and, if never licensed, take an 8-hour safe driving course and present a certificate.

questions.q: A 17-year-old who holds a valid driver's license from another state moves to Connecticut and applies for a Connecticut license. What does the manual require?
options: The eight-hour safe driving practices course, which is also required of 16- and 17-year-old licensed drivers from out of state
Nothing further, since a valid out-of-state license already shows that the teen has completed all required driver training
Only the 30 hours of classroom instruction, because the eight-hour course applies to first-time applicants who hold a permit
A 180-day wait after a Connecticut learner's permit is issued, because the out-of-state license does not count for teens
questions.ref: p.6 Home Training Program: the eight-hour course requirement is also necessary for 16- and 17-year-old licensed drivers from out-of-state who wish to obtain a license in Connecticut.

questions.q: During months seven through twelve after licensing, which passengers may a 16-year-old new driver carry in addition to those allowed in the first six months?
options: Any licensed driver over age 18
Friends of the driver who are also 16 or 17, up to the number of seat belts
Anyone, as long as each passenger has a seat belt
Members of the driver's immediate family
questions.ref: p.8 During the second six months the only additional passengers allowed are members of the driver's immediate family.

questions.q: A 16-year-old is convicted for the second time of violating the passenger restrictions. What is the suspension?
options: A 90-day suspension with a $175 license restoration fee
A 6-month suspension, or until age 18, whichever is longer
A 30-day suspension plus a $175 restoration fee and court fines
A 1-year suspension with a $175 license restoration fee
questions.ref: p.34 GDL violations: 1st offense 30-day suspension; 2nd and subsequent offenses 6-month suspension or until age 18, whichever is longer.

questions.q: A driver wearing a seat belt is stopped with an adult passenger who is not buckled. What does Connecticut law say?
options: Only the passenger can be cited, because the driver is buckled
Only the driver can be cited, since the driver is responsible for the vehicle
Neither can be cited if the vehicle is equipped with airbags
Both the driver and the passenger can be cited, each fined $75
questions.ref: p.12-13 If either driver or passenger fails to wear the seat belt, each could be cited and fined $75; belts are required even with airbags.

questions.q: The DMV sends you a warning notice that insurance coverage on your registered vehicle has lapsed, and you ignore it. What happens?
options: The insurance company reinstates your coverage automatically after 30 days without further action
Your registration is suspended, and the vehicle cannot legally be operated on public highways
Your driver's license is suspended for 45 days and you must complete a retraining program
Your registration stays valid and you are only fined, with no other action taken against you
questions.ref: p.13 Failure to respond to the warning notice results in suspension of registration; a vehicle cannot be operated legally without registration.

questions.q: Before a long road trip, you want to check your tire pressure with a gauge. Where does the manual say you can find the recommended psi?
options: In the vehicle owner's manual or on the driver's side door jamb of the vehicle
On the tire's tread wear indicator, which also shows you how much of the tread has been worn away on the tire
On the registration card that you are required to carry in the vehicle whenever you operate it on a public road
On the dashboard warning light that comes on to show how many pounds per square inch each tire is holding
questions.ref: p.11 Tires: use a tire pressure gauge and the recommended psi located in the vehicle owner's manual or on the driver's side door jamb.

questions.q: Which statement about steering technique is correct?
options: Let the wheel slip back through your fingers after a turn so it straightens on its own
Keep your hands at 12 and 6 o'clock on the wheel so you have the most control in turns
Use hand-over-hand on sharp corners, and straighten the wheel by hand when the turn is done
Use push/pull steering with your hands crossing at the top of the wheel for more control
questions.ref: p.14 Hand-over-hand for sharp corners; straighten by hand - letting it slip through your fingers is dangerous. Hands at 8-10 and 2-4; push/pull hands never cross.

questions.q: Which situation does NOT call for a four-second following distance?
options: Following a motorcycle on a wet metal bridge grating
Following a passenger car on a dry road in light daytime traffic
Pulling a trailer
The driver behind you wants to pass
questions.ref: p.21 Four-second rule applies for slippery roads, driver behind wants to pass, motorcycles, drivers who cannot see you, pulling a trailer, etc.; normal conditions use the three-second rule.

questions.q: You are on a two-lane road with no right lane to move into, and a driver is tailgating you. What should you do?
options: Wait until the road ahead is clear, then reduce speed slowly
Brake firmly so the tailgater backs off
Speed up a few mph to build distance
Tap your brakes repeatedly and flash your high beams
questions.ref: p.22 Being tailgated: if no right lane, wait until the road ahead is clear, then reduce speed slowly; never slow down quickly to discourage a tailgater.

questions.q: Your view ahead is blocked by a hill. You should not start to pass if you are within how far of the hill?
options: 400 feet (about 4 seconds)
One-quarter mile (about 12 seconds)
One-third of a mile (about 10 seconds)
One city block
questions.ref: p.24 Hills and curves: see at least one-third of a mile (about 10 seconds) ahead; do not start to pass if within one-third mile of a hill or curve.

questions.q: At an unmarked intersection, a pedestrian steps to the curb and raises a hand toward oncoming traffic. What must you do?
options: Continue through, since an unmarked intersection does not have a crosswalk for pedestrians
Continue, because pedestrians must first step into the roadway before drivers need to yield
Wait only if the pedestrian actually steps off the curb into the path of your vehicle
Slow or stop and grant the right-of-way; every intersection has a crosswalk even if unmarked
questions.ref: p.16 There is a crosswalk at every intersection even if unmarked; yield when a pedestrian steps to the curb and raises hand and arm toward oncoming traffic.

questions.q: You are driving through a busy neighborhood. Which pedestrians does the manual say are the most frequent victims in auto-pedestrian collisions?
options: Teenagers and young adults, who tend to cross the road quickly and without looking at the oncoming traffic
Children, the elderly, and disabled pedestrians, who may have poor vision and hearing or may move slowly
Commuters walking to work, because they cross during rush hours when the drivers around them are in a hurry
Adults pushing strollers or carts, because the stroller or cart hides the person from the view of the drivers
questions.ref: p.16 Pedestrians: be especially alert for children, the elderly, and disabled pedestrians; they are the most frequent victims in auto-pedestrian collisions.

questions.q: A motorcycle approaching an intersection has its turn signal flashing. What should you do before pulling out in front of it?
options: Pull out, because a flashing signal shows it is turning
Pull out after giving a light tap on the horn
Pull out, because motorcycle signals cancel automatically
Wait until it actually begins to turn
