questions.ref: p.18 Do not assume a motorcycle is turning when its signal flashes; signals may not self-cancel. Do not pull out until you see it begin to turn.

questions.q: Which action is illegal when approaching or passing a horse being ridden on a public road?
options: Reducing your speed and, if necessary, stopping
Sounding your horn or causing loud or unusual noises
Driving at a reasonable speed and a reasonable distance from the horse
Exercising due care as you approach a horse being led along the road
questions.ref: p.18 It is illegal to sound your horn or cause loud or unusual noises when approaching or passing a horse.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT listed as a vulnerable user under Connecticut's Vulnerable User's Law?
options: A person riding or driving an animal
A highway worker
A taxi driver
A wheelchair user
questions.ref: p.16 Vulnerable users: pedestrians, bicyclists, wheelchair users, persons riding or driving an animal, highway workers, garbage trucks, tank vehicles, mail vehicles, express delivery carriers.

questions.q: On a wet road you feel your tires lose traction with the surface. What should you do?
options: Ease off the gas, keep the wheel straight, and avoid stopping or turning until the tires grip
Brake firmly to slow down as quickly as possible, then steer back toward your lane
Turn sharply toward the shoulder in order to leave the standing water as soon as you can
Accelerate gently so that the vehicle can power its way through the water on the road
questions.ref: p.25 If tires lose traction: ease foot off gas, keep steering straight, do not try to stop or turn until tires grip.

questions.q: A hostile motorist is pursuing you after a road dispute. What does the manual recommend?
options: Drive home so you can call the police from safety
Drive to a police station, convenience store, or other well-lit public location
Pull over and get out to calm the other driver down
Pull onto a quiet side street and wait for the driver to pass
questions.ref: p.26 If a motorist pursues you, do not go home; drive to a police station, convenience store or other public, well-lit location.

questions.q: An adult driver over 21 is arrested for DUI and refuses to submit to the chemical test. Compared with an adult who takes and fails the test, the minimum ignition interlock requirement is:
options: Shorter: at least six months rather than at least one year
The same: at least six months in both cases
Not required, since a refusal results only in a suspension
Longer: at least one year rather than at least six months
questions.ref: p.33 Fail test: suspension at least 45 days, IID at least six months. Refuse test (regardless of age): at least 45 days, IID at least one year.

questions.q: A friend who has had several drinks says he will be fine to drive after coffee, fresh air, and a cold shower. According to the manual:
options: Coffee will help him sober up, but a cold shower or fresh air will not make a difference
Fresh air and exercise will sober him up within about an hour, so he can drive safely
Only time will sober him up; coffee, fresh air, exercise, and cold showers do not help
A cold shower and fresh air will help, provided that he waits at least 30 minutes first
questions.ref: p.33 There is no way to sober up quickly. Coffee, fresh air, exercise, or cold showers will not help. Time is the only thing.

questions.q: You are circulating inside a roundabout and a driver at a yield sign is waiting to enter from another leg. What should you do?
options: Continue through; do not stop inside the roundabout, because entering traffic must yield
Stop in the roundabout to let the entering driver go ahead
Yield to the entering vehicle because it is on your right
Slow down and use your left signal to show you are staying in the circle
questions.ref: p.37 Entering traffic must yield to circulating traffic; do not stop within the roundabout to allow traffic to enter from another leg.

questions.q: Your brakes stop working and pumping the pedal several times does not help. What does the manual say to do next?
options: Shift into neutral and turn the ignition off so the engine stops driving the wheels
Pull the parking brake hard and hold it until the vehicle comes to a complete stop
Pull the parking brake slowly, ready to release it if the vehicle begins to skid
Shift into park immediately so the transmission locks the wheels and stops the vehicle
questions.ref: p.39 Brake failure: pump pedal; if that fails use the parking brake, pulling slowly so rear wheels do not lock; then shift to lower gears.

questions.q: Which statement about sign colors is FALSE?
options: Blue signs tell about services along the roadway
Orange signs alert you to dangers from construction and maintenance projects
Green signs tell you where you are, which way to go, and the distance
Brown signs warn of construction and maintenance projects
questions.ref: p.47 Orange = construction/maintenance warnings; brown = parks and recreation; blue = services; green = guide signs.

questions.q: Which pavement marking prohibits lane changing?
options: A dashed white line
A double solid white line
A dashed yellow line alongside a solid yellow line
Double dashed yellow lines
questions.ref: p.44 Other Markings: a double solid white line prohibits lane changing.

questions.q: A white, X-shaped sign reading "Railroad Crossing" is located at a crossing. It has the same meaning as which sign?
options: A yield sign
A stop sign
A pedestrian crossing sign
A flashing yellow light
questions.ref: p.52 Railroad Crossbuck has the same meaning as a Yield sign; you must yield to crossing trains.

questions.q: An applicant who is blind in one eye takes the vision test. What must the other eye meet?
options: At least 20/20 vision with a visual field of 70 degrees
At least 20/40 vision with a visual field of 180 degrees
At least 20/30 vision with a visual field of 100 degrees
At least 20/40 vision with a minimal visual field of 100 degrees or more
questions.ref: p.5 Minimum vision is 20/40; if blind in one eye the other must be at least 20/40 with a minimal visual field of 100 degrees or more.

questions.q: An applicant reads road signs clearly but cannot spot vehicles beside the car while looking straight ahead. Which part of the Connecticut eye test measures this ability?
options: Acuity, which measures how clearly you can see objects directly in front of you on the road ahead
Night vision, which measures how well you can see in the dark and cope with glare from oncoming headlights
Peripheral vision, which measures how far you can see to either side while looking straight ahead
Depth perception, which measures how well you judge the distances and speeds of other vehicles around you
questions.ref: p.5 The Vision Test: the eye test evaluates acuity (how clearly you see) and peripheral vision (how far you can see to either side while looking straight ahead).

questions.q: Which vehicle may an applicant who does not hold a valid driver's license use for the road test?
options: A rental car, as long as the applicant holds a valid learner's permit and is accompanied
A friend's properly insured vehicle that is not currently registered with the DMV
A long-term leased vehicle with insurance identifying the vehicle and the lease company
Any suitable vehicle, if the applicant drives it to the test location alone
questions.ref: p.7 Long-term leased vehicles with proper insurance may be used; you cannot test in a rented vehicle without a valid license; vehicle must be registered and insured; a non-licensed operator cannot drive to the test alone.

questions.q: A 17-year-old is convicted of reckless driving for the second time. What does DMV impose?
options: A 6-month suspension, a $175 license restoration fee, and court fines or imprisonment of not more than 30 days, or both
A 1-year suspension, a $175 license restoration fee, and court fines or imprisonment of not more than one year, or both
A 90-day suspension, a $175 license restoration fee, and court fines but no possibility of imprisonment for the violation
A 6-month suspension or until age 18, whichever is longer, a $175 license restoration fee, and court fines for the violation
questions.ref: p.34 Suspension table: reckless driving 2nd offense is a 1-year suspension, $175 restoration fee, and court fines or imprisonment of not more than one year, or both.

questions.q: A child is 6 years old and weighs 45 pounds. Which restraint meets the manual's requirement?
options: A rear-facing car seat only
The vehicle's seat belt alone
A 5-point harness or a booster seat
A rear-facing convertible seat in the front seat
questions.ref: p.12 Age 5 to 8, or weighing between 40-60 pounds: 5-point harness or booster seat.

questions.q: Which statement about seat belts is supported by the manual?
options: Over half of all traffic deaths happen within 25 miles of home
Airbags protect you in side and rear crashes, so the lap belt is optional
When a vehicle is struck from the side, passengers slide away from the point of impact
It takes about 30 seconds to undo a safety belt
questions.ref: p.13 Over half of all traffic deaths happen within 25 miles of home; belts are required even with airbags; occupants slide toward the crash point; undoing a belt takes less than a second.

questions.q: You must sit in your parked vehicle with the motor running for a long time. What does the manual advise?
options: Close all windows and run the heater
Park inside a closed garage to stay warm
Keep the car in gear with the parking brake off
Open a window
questions.ref: p.12 Never run the motor in a closed garage; if you sit in a vehicle with the motor running for a long time, open a window (leaking exhaust can cause death).

questions.q: You arrive at an intersection where the traffic signal is dark because of a power failure. What does state law require?
options: Treat it as a flashing yellow light and proceed with caution
Stop as though the intersection were controlled by a stop sign
Yield to traffic on your right and proceed if clear
Proceed as if the light were green if you are on the main road
questions.ref: p.15, 25 State law requires a driver at an intersection with an inoperative stop light to stop as though controlled by a stop sign.

questions.q: You need to move across three lanes on a multi-lane road. What does the manual advise?
options: Cross all lanes at once after a single check over your shoulder in the direction of travel
Wait in your lane until every lane is completely clear at the same time, then cross
Change lanes quickly with a signal, since only the lane right next to you matters
Move one lane at a time, checking mirrors, blind spot, and the far lane each time
questions.ref: p.23 Take one lane at a time; check the far lane; waiting until all lanes are clear can tie up traffic and cause a crash.

questions.q: You are on a multi-lane road and the driver ahead of you in the left-most lane is going slower than you want to go. Why does the manual advise against passing that driver on the right?
options: The left-most lane is reserved for vehicles traveling faster than the posted speed limit, so passing on the right is a violation
Passing on the right is permitted only when the driver ahead has signaled a left turn, so any other use risks a collision
The other driver may have difficulty seeing you and might suddenly change lanes in front of you
Vehicles in the right lane always have the right-of-way over passing traffic, so you would have to yield to every one of them
questions.ref: p.23 On Multi-Lane roads: the left-most lane is for passing slower vehicles; if you pass on the right, the other driver may have difficulty seeing you and might suddenly change lanes in front of you.

questions.q: You are on a highway entrance ramp, and traffic on the main road is heavy with no gap yet. What should you do?
options: Slow down on the ramp so you have room to speed up before merging
Drive to the end of the ramp and stop there until a gap in traffic appears
Stop on the ramp and wait until the traffic on the main road has cleared
Cross several lanes quickly once you reach the main road to get past the traffic
questions.ref: p.20 Do not drive to the end of the ramp and stop; if you must wait for space, slow down on the ramp so you have room to speed up before merging.

questions.q: You are in the middle of an intersection when you hear a siren approaching. What must you do?
options: Stop immediately where you are, even inside the intersection
Drive through the intersection first, then pull to the right and stop
Pull to the left edge of the road and stop
Continue driving at the same speed until the vehicle passes
questions.ref: p.37 If you are in an intersection, drive through the intersection before you pull over to the right and stop.

questions.q: A tractor-trailer ahead of you in the right lane approaches an intersection with its right turn signal on, and there is open space between the truck and the curb. What should you do?
options: Stay behind it and do not pass on the right, because it may swing left first and then turn right
Pass on the right quickly before the truck begins to turn
Move alongside the truck's right side where the driver can see you in the mirror
Tap your horn and pass between the truck and the curb
questions.ref: p.20 Resist the temptation to pass on the right of a truck approaching an intersection; you could be caught between the truck and the curb.

questions.q: In which situation may you drive in a designated bicycle lane?
options: When approaching a right turn at an intersection
When passing a slower vehicle in your lane
When entering or leaving an alley or driveway
When avoiding stopped traffic
questions.ref: p.17 Do not stop, park or drive in a bike lane unless entering/leaving an alley or driveway, official duties, directed by police, or emergency; you may turn across but not drive in the lane approaching a turn.

questions.q: You are behind a slow-moving farm tractor with an orange triangle on its back, in a no-passing zone marked by a double solid yellow line. When may you pass it?
options: Never, because passing across a double yellow line is always prohibited
Anytime, because the tractor travels 25 mph or less
Whenever you honk first to warn the tractor driver
Only if you can see far enough ahead to make the pass safely
questions.ref: p.18 State law permits passing slow-moving traffic in no-passing zones; you may cross a double yellow line but must be able to see far enough ahead to pass safely.

questions.q: It is Saturday afternoon and you approach a school with flashing lights warning of a school zone. What does the manual say?
options: Ignore the reduced limit on weekends, because school is not in session that day
Obey the slower posted limit, because school hours are not the only time children are present
Slow down only if you actually see children near the road or at the crosswalk
Slow down only until you have passed the crossing guard, then resume normal speed
questions.ref: p.16 School hours are not the only time children are present; you must obey the slower posted speed limit in school zones.

questions.q: It is raining and the road is wet. Which statement about tire traction is correct according to the manual?
options: Most tires keep good traction at any speed on a wet road as long as you stay in the center of your lane and avoid braking
Most tires have good traction up to about 55 mph, and only badly worn tires begin to ride up on the water below that speed
Most tires have good traction up to about 35 mph, but bald or badly worn tires lose traction at much lower speeds
Most tires lose their traction above about 20 mph, so you should slow to a crawl whenever the pavement is wet at all
questions.ref: p.25 Water on the Roadway: on wet roads most tires have good traction up to about 35 mph; faster, they ride up on water (hydroplaning); bald or badly worn tires lose traction at much lower speeds.

questions.q: You know that you tend to be impatient when you are short on time. Before your next trip, what does the manual suggest?
options: Drive slightly faster than the flow of traffic to make up time
Change lanes often to find the fastest lane
Play loud music to calm down
Give yourself extra time and leave a few minutes early
questions.ref: p.28 If you are impatient, give yourself extra time and leave a few minutes early; do not drive faster than the flow of traffic.

questions.q: Which offense can NOT be considered for youthful offender status when committed by someone under 18?
options: Driving under the influence of alcohol or drugs
Street racing
Reckless driving
Operating while under suspension
questions.ref: p.35 Cannot be a youthful offender: negligent homicide, evading responsibility after death/serious injury, DUI of alcohol or drugs.

questions.q: Which driver must complete a DMV-certified operator retraining program?
options: A 26-year-old with two moving violations
A 23-year-old with two moving violations
A 30-year-old with two moving violations
A 25-year-old with two moving violations
questions.ref: p.35 Age 24 or younger with two or more moving or suspension violations must complete retraining; age 25 or older with three or more.

questions.q: You are making a legal U-turn after giving a left turn signal, stopping, and checking for approaching traffic. Which lane do you enter?
options: The inside (left-hand) lane, nearest the center line
The center lane if the road has more than two lanes
Whichever lane is open
The outside (right-hand) lane traveling in the opposite direction
questions.ref: p.37 U-turns: give a left turn signal, stop, check for traffic, and proceed into the outside or right-hand lane traveling in the opposite direction.

questions.q: At midday a light rain begins and you switch on your windshield wipers. What else must you do?
options: Turn on your headlights, because the law requires them whenever wipers are on
Nothing else is needed, because it is still daytime and the rain is light
Switch on only your parking lights so that other drivers can see your vehicle
Switch on only your fog lights, which are enough for rain in the daytime
questions.ref: p.38 Remember, if you turn on your wipers, turn on your headlights. It's the law. Parking lights are for parked vehicles only.

questions.q: A square sign with a white horizontal bar inside a red circle is posted at an exit ramp. What does it mean?
options: A one-way street; proceed only in the direction of the arrow
You may not enter this road opening
The road is closed ahead; follow the detour
Yield to traffic in the intersection you are entering
questions.ref: p.47 Do Not Enter: a square sign with a white horizontal line inside a red ball; used at exit ramps, crossovers and one-way streets.

questions.q: Overhead signals above a reversible lane show a steady yellow "X." What does it mean?
options: The lane is open only to vehicles that are making a turn at the next intersection
You may not use the lane at this time, and you must stay out of it
Use of the lane is changing; move out of it as soon as it is safe
You may use the lane beneath the signal, as the direction of traffic is fixed
questions.ref: p.44 Reversible lanes: green arrow = may use; red X = may not; flashing yellow X = turning only; steady yellow X = use is changing, move out when safe.

questions.q: A yellow arrow signal appears while you are waiting to turn in the direction of the arrow. What does it mean?
options: The protection of the green arrow is ending, so prepare to stop
You may turn but must yield to oncoming traffic
No turn is allowed in the direction of the arrow
The signal is malfunctioning, so treat it as a stop sign
questions.ref: p.45 A yellow arrow means the protection of a green arrow is ending; if turning in that direction, prepare to stop.

questions.q: Home training may be done by a parent, grandparent, foster parent or legal guardian, or the spouse of a married minor. If the applicant has none of these, which qualified relative may do the home training?
options: A stepparent
A grandparent
A foster parent or legal guardian
The spouse of a married minor applicant
questions.ref: p.6 If the applicant has none of the primary instructors, a qualified uncle or aunt, brother or sister, or stepparent may do the home training.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT among the additional restrictions on learner's permit holders and 16- and 17-year-old licensed drivers?
options: Using a cell phone, even a hands-free one
Transporting more passengers than there are seat belts
Driving on limited-access highways
Operating a vehicle that requires a public passenger transportation permit
questions.ref: p.8 Other restrictions: no more passengers than seat belts, no public passenger/vanpool vehicles, no cell phone even hands-free, no motorcycle passengers for six months.

questions.q: Which 16- or 17-year-old driver is exempt from the passenger and curfew restrictions?
options: A 17-year-old driving friends home from a late school dance on a Friday night
An active volunteer fire company member returning from an emergency call
A 16-year-old whose parents gave written permission for late-night driving
A 17-year-old driver who has held a license for 11 months already
questions.ref: p.8 Passenger and curfew restrictions do not apply to active volunteer fire, ambulance, or EMS members responding to or returning from an emergency call, or Safe Ride assigned drivers.

questions.q: A 17-year-old is convicted for the first time of street racing. What are the consequences?
options: A 6-month suspension and possible imprisonment of not more than 30 days
A 1-year suspension and possible imprisonment of not more than one year
A 60-day suspension and a $175 restoration fee only
A 6-month suspension and possible imprisonment of not more than one year
questions.ref: p.34 Street racing 1st offense: 6-month suspension, $175 restoration fee, court fines or imprisonment of not more than one year (reckless driving 1st offense is up to 30 days).

questions.q: Besides emergency calls, which driver may use a hand-held cell phone or mobile electronic device under the law's exception?
options: A 30-year-old taxi driver
A 19-year-old ambulance driver
A 25-year-old delivery driver
A 40-year-old school bus driver
questions.ref: p.13 Drivers 18 and older who are peace officers, firefighters, or ambulance drivers may use hand-held cell phones and electronic devices.

questions.q: Which child restraint placement is prohibited by Connecticut law?
options: A forward-facing seat with a 5-point harness in the back seat of the vehicle
A rear-facing convertible seat placed in the back seat of the vehicle
A booster seat in the back seat for a 9-year-old child weighing 65 pounds
A rear-facing restraint in the front seat of a vehicle with a functional passenger airbag
questions.ref: p.12 The law prohibits the placement of a rear-facing child restraint system in the front seat of a vehicle with a functional passenger side airbag.

questions.q: During what period are studded tires permitted in Connecticut?
options: November 15 through April 30
October 1 through April 15
December 1 through March 31
November 1 through May 15
questions.ref: p.25 Studded tires are permitted in Connecticut from November 15th through April 30th.

questions.q: In a Connecticut work zone, which offense carries doubled fines?
options: Speeding through the work zone at more than the reduced posted speed limit
Using an improper lane while driving through the work zone itself
Illegally using a hand-held cellphone or mobile electronic device
Disobeying traffic control devices posted in the work zone, such as signs
questions.ref: p.15 Distracted driving fines are doubled for illegally using a hand-held phone in a work zone; speeding/devices/improper lane carry fines up to $1,000 and points.

questions.q: You are approaching a bicyclist who is riding in the travel lane, and you are tempted to sound your horn to announce that you are behind. What does the manual say?
options: Do not sound it close to the bicyclist unless you have good cause, because it may startle the rider into steering into your path
Sound it right away, since a bicyclist in the travel lane has no right to the lane and must move over to the right edge of the road
Sound it twice well ahead of the rider, since bicyclists should be told that a motor vehicle is coming up behind them at speed
Sound it only after you have started passing, so that the bicyclist knows you intend to move back into the lane ahead
questions.ref: p.17 As a driver: do not sound your horn close to bicyclists unless you have good cause; it may startle them and cause them to steer into your path and crash.

questions.q: Which technique does the manual recommend when you must back your vehicle?
options: Rely mainly on your rear-view and side mirrors, since they show the whole area
Turn and look over your right shoulder, directly through the rear window
Back quickly so that you spend as little time as possible blocking the road
Look only in your side mirrors while turning the wheel quickly in both directions
questions.ref: p.24 Turn around and look over your right shoulder; do not depend on mirrors; back slowly.

questions.q: Where there are no signs or lane markings controlling a turn, from which lane should you turn, and into which lane?
options: From the center lane, into the farthest lane
From the lane closest to the direction you want to go, into the lane farthest from the one you came from
From the right lane in every case, into the left lane
From the lane closest to the direction you want to go, into the lane closest to the one you came from
questions.ref: p.23 Turn from the lane closest to the direction you want to go and into the lane closest to the one you came from to cross the fewest lanes.

questions.q: An ice cream truck with flashing lights and its stop arm extended is in a lane on the other side of a road separated by a physical barrier. What must you do?
options: Stop at least 10 feet away and then pass at no more than 5 mph, yielding to pedestrians
Stop at least 25 feet from the front of the truck and wait for the lights to stop
You need not stop, because the truck is in a lane separated by a physical barrier
Stop until the truck's lights stop flashing, then proceed with caution
questions.ref: p.18 Drivers are not required to stop and proceed this way for an ice cream truck in another lane separated by a safety island or physical barrier.

questions.q: A person pushes the front wheels of a stroller into the entrance of a crosswalk as your vehicle approaches. What must you do?
options: Continue, because the pedestrian is not yet fully in the crosswalk
Slow or stop and grant the right-of-way to the pedestrian
Continue unless the pedestrian raises a hand toward you
Sound your horn so the pedestrian waits
questions.ref: p.16 A pedestrian indicates intent to cross by moving any extension of the body, including a stroller, into the crosswalk entrance; drivers must slow or stop and grant right-of-way.

questions.q: Which statement about motorcycles is TRUE?
options: Motorcycles can stop quickly, so following too closely endangers the rider
Motorcycle turn signals always cancel automatically
You may pass a motorcycle within its lane if there is room
You do not need to dim your high beams for a motorcycle, since it is small
questions.ref: p.18 Motorcycles can stop quickly; signals may not self-cancel; do not pass in the same lane; always dim headlights when approaching a motorcycle.

questions.q: You are passing a tractor-trailer. What does the manual advise about returning to your lane?
options: Return as soon as you pass the cab, then slow down to give the truck some room
Return once you see the front of the truck, then slow down to let the truck go by
Signal and return when you see the front of the truck in your inside mirror; keep your speed up
Stay alongside the cab until the truck driver signals that it is safe for you to go
questions.ref: p.19 Signal and return to the right lane when you can see the front of the truck in your inside mirror; after passing, keep your speed up.

questions.q: A bicyclist ahead on a gravel-strewn road keeps both hands on the handlebars and gives no hand signal. What should you do?
options: Assume the bicyclist will continue straight ahead, since no turn has been signaled
Sound your horn so the bicyclist will give a signal to show where they are headed
Pass immediately, before the bicyclist has a chance to move into the lane ahead
Look for other clues, such as the bicyclist turning or looking over a shoulder
questions.ref: p.17 A bicyclist may be unable to signal if conditions require both hands on the handlebars; look for other clues like turning head or looking over shoulder.

questions.q: You are approaching a sharp curve at higher speed than is comfortable. What does the manual advise?
options: Slow down before you enter the curve so you do not have to brake in it
Brake in the curve if the speed starts to feel too high once you are inside it
Speed up slightly in the curve so that the tires gain more traction on the road
Shift to neutral in the curve so that the vehicle slows without using the brakes
questions.ref: p.25 Always slow down before you enter the curve so you do not have to brake in the curve; braking in a curve can cause a skid.

questions.q: The driver ahead of you drifts over the lane lines and appears busy with a map. What does the manual advise?
options: Stay about two seconds behind so you can closely watch the driver's behavior
Give the driver plenty of room and keep a following distance of 3 to 4 seconds
Pass immediately on the right to get ahead of the driver as soon as possible
Tap your horn repeatedly to get the driver's attention back on the road ahead
questions.ref: p.27 Give a distracted driver plenty of room and maintain a safe following distance of 3 to 4 seconds; be very careful when passing.

questions.q: You are pulled over by police at night. Which action is NOT recommended?
options: Turning on the interior light after stopping and before the officer approaches your car
Keeping your hands on the steering wheel while the officer approaches
Reaching for license and registration as soon as you stop, before being asked
Keeping all doors closed and staying in the vehicle unless asked to get out
questions.ref: p.35 Obtain your driver license and/or registration only when requested; keep hands on wheel; turn on interior light at night.

questions.q: You took an over-the-counter allergy medicine and are not sure it is safe to drive. What does the manual advise?
options: Drink a cup of coffee, which will offset any drowsiness that the medicine may cause
Assume it is safe to drive, because it is sold without a prescription at stores
Drive, but stay on roads with posted limits below 45 mph until the drowsiness ends
Check the label for warnings, and if still unsure, ask your doctor or pharmacist
questions.ref: p.33 Check the label for warnings; if not sure whether it is safe to take the drug and drive, ask your doctor or pharmacist.

questions.q: You must slow down to turn off a roadway that has no separate turn or exit lane, at a spot where the driver behind you will not expect it. What does the manual advise?
options: Turn on your emergency flashers and slow down gradually until you reach the turn, so that traffic behind you can see them
Brake as hard as needed at the last moment, since your brake lights alone will warn the driver behind you in time
Tap your brake pedal quickly three or four times to let those behind you know you are about to slow down
Signal for the turn as soon as you can see it, since an early signal lets the drivers behind you react before you slow
questions.ref: p.39 Signal When You Slow Down: if you will slow at a place where a driver does not expect it (such as turning off a roadway with no separate turn lane), tap your brake pedal quickly three or four times.

questions.q: At a crash scene with several injured people, whom do you help first and what do you check first?
options: People who are not walking and talking; check breathing first, then bleeding
Anyone who is bleeding; check for broken bones first, then breathing
People who are walking and talking; check for bleeding first, then breathing
The driver of the nearest vehicle; check how alert the person is before anything
questions.ref: p.41 First help anyone who is not already walking and talking. Check for breathing, and then check for bleeding.

questions.q: A pentagon-shaped school sign has a separate downward-pointing arrow plaque. What does the plaque indicate?
options: The direction of school bus loading
The place where the reduced speed zone ends
The location of the school building
The actual location of the crosswalk
questions.ref: p.46 Pentagon: school zone/crossing; may have separate downward-pointing arrow plaque indicating the actual location of the crosswalk.

questions.q: A center lane is marked on each side by a solid yellow line and a dashed yellow line, with left-turn arrows for one direction alternating with arrows for the other direction. What is it?
options: A reversible lane that carries traffic in only one direction at a time
A shared center lane for left turns, used by traffic from both directions
A passing lane that is open to traffic in both directions at the same time
A lane reserved for high occupancy vehicles during rush hours only
questions.ref: p.44 Shared Center Lane: reserved for left turns (or U-turns when permitted), used by traffic in both directions, marked by solid and dashed yellow lines with alternating arrows.

questions.q: You approach an intersection controlled by a single flashing red traffic light. What does it mean?
options: Slow down and proceed with caution
Stop only if cross traffic is present
Yield to cross traffic and continue without stopping
Come to a full stop, then proceed when it is safe to do so
questions.ref: p.45 A flashing red traffic light means the same as a stop sign; you must come to a full stop and may proceed when it is safe.

questions.q: According to the DMV Commissioner's Advisory Committee on Teen Safe Driving, what is the number one cause of death for teenagers aged 15 to 19?
options: Swimming and boating accidents
Sports and recreation injuries
Motor vehicle crashes
Drug and alcohol overdoses
questions.ref: p.4 Managing Your Teen's Driving Experience: motor vehicle crashes are the #1 cause of death for 15-19 year-old teenagers.

questions.q: A parent asks when most teen crashes happen. According to the manual, most teen crashes occur during which period?
options: The third and fourth years of driving
The first two years of having a license
The year right after the teen turns 18
The first two months with a permit
questions.ref: p.4 Managing Your Teen's Driving Experience: most teen crashes occur during the first two years of having their license (the first six months are the most dangerous).

questions.q: Research cited in the manual says the part of the brain that assesses risk and danger is not fully developed until about what age?
options: Age 18
Age 16
The late teens
The mid 20s
questions.ref: p.4 Brain Development: the portion of the brain that assesses risk and danger does not fully develop until the mid 20's.

questions.q: A newly licensed teen says it is safe to drive three younger siblings to the mall because they are family, not friends. What does the manual say about this?
options: Siblings do not raise crash risk the way that teenage friends in the car do
Crash risk rises with the number of passengers, siblings included
Crash risk rises only when passengers are over age 16
More passengers lower the risk because extra eyes help watch the road
questions.ref: p.4 Passenger Restrictions: crash risk goes up with teen passengers and increases with the number of passengers, whether siblings, family or friends.

questions.q: According to the manual, which group of people has the lowest rate of seatbelt use?
options: Rear-seat adult passengers
Drivers over age 65
Commercial truck drivers
Teens
questions.ref: p.4 It's the Law: Require Your Teen to Buckle Up: teens have the lowest rate of seatbelt use.

questions.q: A family is choosing a car for their newly licensed 16-year-old. Which choice follows the manual's advice?
options: Any model is fine for a teen as long as it has recently passed its emissions test
Pick a high-performance car so the teen can speed up out of trouble
Avoid high-performance cars and older models lacking newer safety technology
Pick an older, heavier model, because older cars are always the safest in a crash
questions.ref: p.4 Vehicle Selection Matters: avoid having your teen drive high performance vehicles or older model vehicles that lack improved safety technologies.

questions.q: Why does the manual urge parents to restrict their teen's night driving?
options: Fatal crashes are likelier at night, and young drivers risk drowsy driving
Most teen tickets are written at night, which raises the family's insurance rates
The road test is given only in daylight, so teens get no practice at night
Headlights do not work as well on newer cars, and roads are not lit outside of cities
questions.ref: p.4 Restrict Night Driving: fatal crashes are more likely to occur at night; young drivers are at higher risk for drowsy driving.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the distracting activities the manual lists as raising a teen's risk of a serious crash?
options: Having an unrestrained pet in the car
Dialing different radio stations
Checking the mirrors often
Talking with other passengers
questions.ref: p.4 Teach your Teen About Distracted Driving: talking on the phone or with passengers, texting, dialing radio stations, unrestrained pets and other distractions increase crash risk.

questions.q: A non-commercial Connecticut driver's license is known and designated as which class?
options: Class M
Class A
Class C
Class D
questions.ref: p.4 Obtaining a Learner's Permit: a non-commercial driver's license is known and designated as Class D.

questions.q: Unless restrictions appear on it, a Class D license may be used to operate which vehicles?
options: Any motor vehicle, including buses and big trucks
Any motor vehicle except a commercial motor vehicle
Any motor vehicle except a manual-transmission car
Passenger cars only, and not pickup trucks or vans
questions.ref: p.4 Obtaining a Learner's Permit: unless restrictions appear, a Class D license may be used to operate any motor vehicle except a commercial motor vehicle.

questions.q: You already have a Class D license and want to add an endorsement to ride a motorcycle. Which manual does the DMV say you need to read?
options: The Motorcycle Operator's manual
Only the Class D driver's manual
The Public Service Vehicle manual
The Commercial Driver's License manual
questions.ref: p.4 Obtaining a Learner's Permit: for a motorcycle endorsement you need to read the Motorcycle Operator's manual; trucks and buses need the CDL manual.

questions.q: A 16-year-old with a learner's permit is about to practice with a qualified parent but left the permit at home. What does the manual require?
options: The permit can stay at home as long as the parent has a valid license
The permit is needed only when driving on a highway
The permit must be carried whenever the permit holder is driving
The permit is needed only for the road test, not for practice drives at home
questions.ref: p.4 First Time Drivers: a permit holder must carry a learner's permit whenever he or she is operating a vehicle.

questions.q: An applicant has a medical condition that may affect safe driving. When must a favorable review of the condition be obtained?
options: Before the learner's permit is issued
Only if the applicant later has a crash
Before the first license renewal
Within 90 days after the road test
questions.ref: pp.4-5 First Time Drivers: an applicant with such conditions must undergo a review; a favorable review must be obtained prior to issuance of the learner's permit.

questions.q: A 15-year-old wants to get a Connecticut learner's permit. What does the manual say?
options: She may get it if she passes with 23 correct
She must wait until she is at least 16
She may get it if a parent takes parent training
She may get it if she enrolls in driving school
questions.ref: p.5 To obtain a learner's permit: you must be at least 16 years of age.

questions.q: To obtain a learner's permit, which tests must you pass?
options: A vision test and a 25-question knowledge test
A hearing test and a 25-item knowledge test
A road test and a 25-question knowledge test
A vision test and a 50-question knowledge test
questions.ref: p.5 To obtain a learner's permit: you must pass both a vision and a 25-question knowledge test.

questions.q: An applicant's vision is 20/50 without glasses and 20/30 with glasses. Does the applicant meet Connecticut's minimum vision requirement?
options: Yes, because 20/40 may be met with glasses or contacts
No, because 20/20 is needed when wearing glasses
No, because 20/40 must be met without wearing any glasses or contacts
Yes, but only for a limited license that allows daylight driving only
questions.ref: p.5 The Vision Test: the minimum vision requirement for all classes of license is at least 20/40 with or without glasses or contact lenses.

questions.q: Which statement about applicants with monocular vision (blind in one eye) is correct?
options: They need 20/20 in the other eye to drive
They cannot get certain special licenses or endorsements
They may never hold any kind of Connecticut driver's license
They may drive only with a licensed parent in the car until age 21
questions.ref: p.5 The Vision Test: persons with monocular vision do not qualify for certain special licenses or endorsements (the other eye must be 20/40 with a 100-degree field).

questions.q: Your side vision lets you notice a car on your right while looking ahead. Why does the manual say you must still use your side mirrors or glance to the side?
options: Because side vision fades at highway speeds
Because you cannot focus on things off to the side
Because mirrors show traffic in front of you
Because the law forbids relying on side vision alone while driving
questions.ref: p.5 Side Vision: because you cannot focus on things to the side, you must also use your side mirrors or glance to the side if necessary.

questions.q: According to the manual, judging distances and speeds well is especially important in which situation?
options: Judging safe openings when passing on two-lane roads
Reading the speed limit signs posted along the interstate highway
Spotting the dashboard warning lights early
Adjusting the mirrors before the road test
questions.ref: p.5 Judging Distances and Speeds: especially important in knowing how far you are from other vehicles and judging safe openings when merging and passing on two-lane roads.

questions.q: A driver who sees well in daylight notices trouble with the glare of oncoming headlights after dark. What does the manual advise?
options: Wear sunglasses at night to cut down on headlight glare
Night driving is fine as long as you passed the vision test at the DMV
Use high beams so that oncoming drivers will dim their own headlights
Don't drive more than necessary at night, and be very careful
questions.ref: p.5 Night Vision: if you have problems seeing at night, don't drive more than is necessary and be very careful when you do.

questions.q: How often does the manual say you should have your eyes checked by an eye specialist?
options: Every year or two
Only when you renew
Every three months
Every five years
questions.ref: p.5 The Vision Test: you should have your eyes checked every year or two by an eye specialist.

questions.q: Which statement about drivers with hearing problems is TRUE according to the manual?
options: Their driving records are much worse, so they need a limited license
They must have a passenger with good hearing ride along whenever they drive
Their driving records are just as good as drivers with good hearing
They may not drive on highways because they cannot hear sirens
questions.ref: p.5 The Vision Test (hearing): studies have shown that the driving records of hearing-impaired drivers are just as good as those of drivers with good hearing.

questions.q: Which statement about hearing and driving is FALSE according to the manual?
options: Hearing loss always comes on suddenly, so drivers notice it right away
The sound of horns, a siren, or screeching tires can warn a driver of danger
Hearing problems, like bad eyesight, can come on very slowly
Deaf drivers learn to rely more on their vision and tend to stay more alert
questions.ref: p.5 Hearing: hearing problems, like bad eyesight, can come on so slowly that you do not notice them; deaf drivers rely more on vision and stay alert.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the ways a 16- or 17-year-old may complete the required driver training program?
options: Home training plus the 8-hour course
Studying this manual alone with no course
A licensed commercial driving school
A secondary school (high school) program
questions.ref: p.6 16- and 17-Year-Old Applicants: training must be through a licensed commercial driving school, a secondary school program, or home training plus the eight-hour safe driving course.

questions.q: A DMV-approved commercial or secondary school driver education program for teens consists of how many hours of classroom instruction?
options: 20 hours
30 hours
8 hours
40 hours
questions.ref: p.6 Commercial Driving School or Secondary School Training: 30 hours of classroom instruction and at least 40 hours of behind-the-wheel training.

questions.q: A teen finishes a commercial driving school course. What document does the school issue that the teen needs to be eligible for the road test?
options: A signed home instructor statement
A temporary paper driver's license
A Medical Review Division clearance letter from DMV
A course completion certificate (form CS-1)
questions.ref: p.6 Commercial Driving School or Secondary School Training: the school will issue a course completion certificate (form CS-1), required to be eligible for the road test.

questions.q: A 16-year-old is home trained by a parent for all 40 hours of driving and takes only the 8-hour safe driving course at a driving school. How long after the permit is issued must she wait to take the road test?
options: 180 days
90 days
120 days
60 days
questions.ref: p.6 Commercial/Secondary and Home Training: applicants without full school driver education (or full 30 hours classroom plus 8 hours school behind-the-wheel) must wait 180 days after the permit is issued.

questions.q: When must a home instructor sign the statement that the applicant got a permit and completed at least 30 hours of course study?
options: When the license card is mailed
When the permit is first issued
Before the knowledge test
At the time of the road test
questions.ref: p.6 Home Training Program: the home instructor must sign a statement at the time of the road test.

questions.q: What must a home training course cover?
options: Only the material that will be scored on the road test checklist
Only the teen driving laws covered in the parent training
All the material in this manual, plus other needed information
Only the road signs and pavement markings chapter of the manual
questions.ref: p.6 Home Training Program: the home training course must cover all of the material in this manual and other necessary driver education information.

questions.q: A home-trained teen must show a course completion certificate for the approved eight-hour course. Which form is it?
options: Form B-230
Form CS-1 a
Form CS-1
Form R-1
questions.ref: p.6 Home Training Program: home-trained applicants must show a course completion certificate (form CS-1 a) from a secondary or commercial driving school.

questions.q: Which statement about the eight-hour safe driving course required of home-trained teens is FALSE?
options: It includes the two-hour mandatory parent training class
It includes at least four hours on alcohol and drugs
It may be taken from the DMV-approved home instructor
It is also required of 16- and 17-year-olds licensed out of state
questions.ref: p.6 Home Training Program: the CS-1 a must come from a local secondary school or commercial driving school; the course includes 4 hours on alcohol/drugs and the 2-hour parent class; also required of out-of-state 16-17 year-old licensed drivers.

questions.q: A 16-year-old completes 25 hours of behind-the-wheel training at a driving school and 15 hours with a qualified parent. Does this meet the 40-hour behind-the-wheel requirement?
options: Yes, any mix of school and home training may be used
No, all 40 hours must be at a driving school
Yes, but only if the parent is a licensed instructor
No, at least 30 hours must be home training
questions.ref: p.7: all 16- and 17-year-old applicants must have at least 40 hours of behind-the-wheel training, which may be any combination of professional (driving school) or home training.

questions.q: Kai is 18 and just got a learner's permit. He wants to practice with his 19-year-old cousin, who has been licensed for three years. Is this allowed?
options: No, an 18-year-old must use a driving school only
Yes, if the cousin's license was never suspended
No, a qualified trainer must be at least 20 years old
Yes, trainer rules no longer apply at age 18
questions.ref: p.7 Applicants 18 Years of Age or Older: the permit holder must be accompanied by a school instructor or a qualified trainer age 20 or older with a license unsuspended for four or more consecutive years.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT listed in the manual as something you should know before you take your road test?
options: When to stop for a yellow signal
How to change a flat tire
How to park properly on a hill
How to control the car in reverse
questions.ref: p.7 Things you should know before you take your test: speed, turning, right of way, stopping for a yellow signal, backing, and parking (including on a hill).

questions.q: You arrive for your road test and are walking to the test vehicle. What does the manual say you should do before getting in?
options: Ask the examiner which route you will take
Look for nearby parked cars, people, or objects
Check the engine oil level and the pressure in each tire
Honk the horn to alert people nearby
questions.ref: p.7 Things you should remember during your test: prior to entering the test vehicle, observe nearby parked cars, people, or objects that could affect your ability to safely put the car in motion.

questions.q: During your road test, the car is in "park" and you are ready to pull out. What should you do before shifting into gear?
options: Release the parking brake
Sound the horn once
Turn on the hazard lights
Apply the brake
questions.ref: p.7 Things you should remember during your test: apply the brake before you shift the car into gear from the "park" position.

questions.q: The examiner asks you to show how you would signal a turn if your turn signals did not work. What does the manual say you should be able to do?
options: Use your four-way hazard lights
Tap your horn twice at the turn
Flash your headlights at traffic
Demonstrate hand signals
questions.ref: p.7 Things you should remember during your test: use the turn signals every time it is appropriate and be able to demonstrate hand signals.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT required for the vehicle you bring to your road test?
options: It must be registered in the applicant's own name
It must be mechanically safe to operate
It must suit the license class applied for
It must have valid proof of insurance with it on test day
questions.ref: p.7 The Road Test: you must appear with a vehicle appropriate for the license class, mechanically safe, with valid registration and proof of insurance (a properly insured long-term leased vehicle may be used).

questions.q: A new driver passes the road test. How much must be paid for the license?
questions.ref: p.7 To Begin the Road Test You Will Need: License Fees - you must pay $84 for a license after you pass the road test.

questions.q: An applicant had a medical condition reviewed before getting a permit. What extra item may this applicant need to begin the road test?
options: A note from the applicant's school nurse
A letter from the applicant's auto insurance agent saying it is covered
A second vision test from an eye doctor
A clearance letter from the DMV Medical Review Division
questions.ref: p.7 To Begin the Road Test You Will Need: a clearance letter from DMV Medical Review Division (only if required, see First Time Drivers).

questions.q: Which item is NOT on the list of things every applicant needs to begin the road test?
options: A diploma from high school
Proof of the 8-hour course
Your current learner's permit
The license fee
questions.ref: p.7 To Begin the Road Test You Will Need: your learner's permit, proof of the 8-hour safe driving course (CS-1), license fees, and a medical clearance letter only if required.

questions.q: During your road test, the examiner asks you to turn on the defroster and then the windshield washers. Why?
options: Operating vehicle equipment is part of the road test
The examiner is checking it for an emissions test
It shows the car passed its safety inspection
It is only done if the test is held in the winter
questions.ref: p.8 The road test evaluates: operation of vehicle equipment such as wipers and washers, heater and defroster, parking brake, headlights and high beams, and the horn.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT listed among the things the road test evaluates?
options: Adjusting the seat and the mirrors
Recognizing warning lights on the panel
Responding to emergency vehicles
Checking the engine oil level
questions.ref: p.8 The road test evaluates: adjusting seat, mirrors, steering wheel and seat belts; operating equipment; response to signs, signals and emergency vehicles; backing/parking; turns; recognizing instrument-panel warning lights; other maneuvers.

questions.q: You are paying your license fee by check at a DMV branch office. To whom should the check be made payable?
options: Your town clerk
The driving school
DMV
The State Treasurer
questions.ref: p.8 Pay for Your License: please make all checks payable to DMV.

questions.q: Two months after getting his license, a 16-year-old wants to drive his mother and father to dinner. Only his mother holds a valid license. Is this allowed?
options: Yes, but only after his first six months
No, both of his parents must hold valid driver's licenses
No, he may not drive his parents together
Yes, if at least one parent holds a valid license
questions.ref: p.8 Passenger Restrictions: during the first six months, passengers may include his or her parents or legal guardian, at least one of whom holds a valid driver's license.

questions.q: Four months after getting her license, a 17-year-old wants to drive two neighbors, both 30 years old and licensed for ten years with no suspensions. Is this allowed?
options: No, only one such qualified adult may ride
Yes, as long as each has a seat belt
Yes, both are over 20 and qualified
No, only a licensed instructor may ride
questions.ref: p.8 Passenger Restrictions: during the first six months, the exception is one person at least 20 years old who has held a license for four or more consecutive years without suspension.

questions.q: A 17-year-old licensed driver leaves home at 5:15 a.m. to go to the gym. Does this violate the curfew?
options: Yes, the curfew lasts until 5:30 a.m.
No, the curfew ends at 5 a.m.
Yes, the curfew ends at 6 a.m.
Yes, gym trips are never allowed
questions.ref: p.8 Hour Restrictions (Curfew): 11 p.m. to 5 a.m.

questions.q: At midnight, a 17-year-old who is an active volunteer ambulance service member drives a friend home from a party. Do the curfew and passenger restrictions apply?
options: Yes, the exemption covers only emergency calls and active duties
No, active volunteer ambulance members are exempt from them at all times
No, as long as the ambulance service gave permission
Yes, but only the curfew applies to him, not the passenger restriction
questions.ref: p.8 Please note: the restrictions do not apply to active volunteer fire, ambulance or EMS members responding to or returning from an emergency call or carrying out duties as an active member.

questions.q: A 17-year-old just got a motorcycle endorsement. For how long may he NOT carry a passenger on a motorcycle?
options: Until his 18th birthday, regardless of the date issued
Three months after the endorsement is issued
Six months after the endorsement is issued
One full year after the endorsement is issued
questions.ref: p.8 Other Restrictions: 16- and 17-year-old drivers may not transport any passenger on a motorcycle for six months after the issuance of a motorcycle endorsement.

questions.q: Ten months after getting his license, a 17-year-old wants to drive his parents and four siblings in a car with five seat belts. Is this allowed?
options: No, he may carry only one sibling at a time
No, he may not carry more passengers than seat belts
Yes, because all of the passengers are members of his immediate family
Yes, since his parents are riding with him
questions.ref: p.8 Passenger Restrictions and Other Restrictions: family is allowed after six months, but 16- and 17-year-olds may not transport more passengers than the number of seatbelts (seven people, five belts).

questions.q: A 17-year-old licensed driver is offered a summer job driving a vanpool vehicle. What does the manual say?
options: It is allowed once the teen is licensed six months
16- and 17-year-olds may not operate a vanpool vehicle
It is allowed if no passenger is under age 18
It is allowed only during daylight hours
questions.ref: p.8 Other Restrictions: 16- and 17-year-old licensed drivers may not operate any vehicle that requires a public passenger transportation permit or a vanpool vehicle.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a way the manual lists to register as an organ and tissue donor?
options: By calling your local hospital
By mail on the Change of Address form
When you obtain or renew a license
Online at the DMV website
questions.ref: p.8 Becoming an Organ and Tissue Donor: register when you obtain or renew a license or ID card, online at ct.gov/dmv, or by mail with DMV's Change of Address form.

questions.q: How much does it cost to be registered as an organ and tissue donor when you get your driver's license?
options: A $10 fee
A $30 fee
Nothing
An $84 fee
questions.ref: p.8 Becoming an Organ and Tissue Donor: there is "no fee" to be registered as an organ and tissue donor.

questions.q: You already have a valid license and want to add the organ donor insignia to it now. What must you do?
options: Order a duplicate credential and pay a $30 fee
Nothing; it is added free at your next renewal visit
Mail a letter to your town hall asking for a sticker
Retake the vision test and pay the $84 license fee
questions.ref: p.8 Becoming an Organ and Tissue Donor: to add or remove the insignia on a valid license or ID, you need to order a duplicate credential and pay a $30.00 duplicate credential fee.

questions.q: For which people is being included in the Organ and Tissue Donor Registry legal authorization for donation?
options: Individuals 21 and over
Individuals 16 and over
Any age, with no limit
Individuals 18 and over
questions.ref: p.8 Becoming an Organ and Tissue Donor: for individuals 18 and over, being included in the Registry is legal authorization for organ and tissue donation.

questions.q: After you sign up as an organ and tissue donor at the DMV, what does the manual ask you to do?
options: Renew the choice every year by mail
Carry a separate donor card at all times
Notify your insurance company in writing
Tell your family about your decision
questions.ref: p.9 (continued from p.8): please be sure to inform your family of your decision to be an organ and tissue donor.

questions.q: You apply for voter registration while renewing your license at the DMV. About how long until you should get a confirmation notice from your town's registrar of voters?
options: About six months
About 60 days
About three weeks
About one week
questions.ref: p.9 Registering to Vote: you should receive a confirmation notice in approximately three (3) weeks from the registrar of voters in your city or town.

questions.q: You move to a new town and file a change of address with the DMV, but you do NOT want it used for voting records. What should you do?
options: Nothing; the DMV never shares any change of address information
Ask the DMV to cancel your current voter registration
File the change of address only after the next election
Indicate on the form that it is not for voter registration
questions.ref: p.9 Registering to Vote: your change of address form will be used to update your voter registration record unless you indicate on the form that it is NOT for voter registration purposes.

questions.q: Which statement about registering to vote through the DMV is correct?
options: You may apply only when you first get a license
You may apply or update your registration at any time
You may apply only in the month before an election
You may apply only at your town's registrar office
questions.ref: p.9 Registering to Vote: you can apply for voter registration or update your information through DMV at any time; you are offered the chance when you apply for, renew or replace a license or ID.

questions.q: You choose to apply for voter registration at the DMV. What does the DMV do next?
options: Gives you a receipt and sends your application to election officials
Gives you a paper form to mail to the governor's office
Registers you itself and then mails your new voter card to you within 20 days
Adds a voter insignia to your license for a $30 fee
questions.ref: p.9 Registering to Vote: DMV will provide you with a receipt and will transmit your voter registration application information to election officials.

questions.q: Who helped the Connecticut DMV develop the Limited Driver's License program?
options: The Office of the Secretary of State
The DMV Commissioner's Advisory Committee on Teen Safe Driving
The Bureau of Rehabilitation Services
Its Medical Advisory Board of volunteer doctors
questions.ref: p.9 Limited Licenses Program: the DMV, with the help of its Medical Advisory Board (medical doctors who volunteer their time), developed the Limited Driver's License program.

questions.q: A driver's physical abilities have changed since she was first licensed. Before a limited license is issued, what may be required?
options: A second 8-hour safe driving course and the CS-1 form
Reports from one or more physicians and an on-road skills test
A signed statement from a licensed home driving instructor
A new 25-question knowledge test and a new photo learner's permit
questions.ref: p.9 Limited Licenses Program: reports made by one or more physicians must be submitted and the person may be required to pass an on-the-road skills test with a DMV inspector.

questions.q: A person with a medical condition that affects driving is moving to Connecticut. How far ahead of applying for a license does the manual recommend contacting the Driver Services Division?
options: At least one year
At least 30 days
At least four months
At least two weeks
questions.ref: p.9 Limited Licenses Program: contact the Driver Services Division at least four months prior to applying for a Connecticut license, whether a new driver or a new resident.

questions.q: Which statement about the Limited Licenses Program is FALSE?
options: It is for people whose physical abilities changed
Its restrictions are noted on the license document
It may require an on-road test with an inspector
It is only for drivers who were already licensed
questions.ref: p.9 Limited Licenses Program: it also allows DMV to issue new licenses to persons who previously would not have qualified; restrictions are noted on the license document.

questions.q: For which type of license holder are the health standards more stringent?
options: A bus or taxi driver carrying passengers
A driver renewing a Class D license
A 16-year-old with a new Class D license
A driver with a daylight-only license
questions.ref: p.9 Limited Licenses Program: health standards are more stringent for CDL holders or holders of a license to operate a vehicle carrying passengers (taxi, delivery vehicle, bus, school bus, etc.).

questions.q: A limited license may restrict a driver to using corrective lenses. Which kind of lenses does this restriction NOT include?
options: Bifocal eyeglasses
Prescription glasses
Telescopic lenses
Soft contact lenses
questions.ref: p.9 Limited Licenses Program: restriction when using corrective lenses (not including telescopic lenses) as prescribed by a licensed optometrist or ophthalmologist.

questions.q: A driver's limited license says she may drive only on highways that are not limited access highways. Which road may she NOT use?
options: A two-lane country road with no exits
A limited access interstate highway
A local road that passes through a school zone
A city street in the town where she lives
questions.ref: p.9 Limited Licenses Program: one restriction permits operation only on highways that are not limited access highways.

questions.q: A limited license may require outside mirrors on both the left and right sides of the vehicle. How far to the rear must those mirrors show the driver a view of the highway?
options: At least 50 feet
At least 200 feet
At least 500 feet
At least 100 feet
questions.ref: p.9 Limited Licenses Program: external mirrors on both left and right sides to reflect a view of the highway at least 200 feet to the rear.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the restrictions a limited license may contain?
options: Driving only with a licensed passenger
Driving only an automatic-shift car
Driving only in the period of daylight
Driving only with special controls
questions.ref: p.9 Limited Licenses Program: listed restrictions are daylight, corrective lenses, non-limited-access highways, automatic transmission, left and right external mirrors, and special controls or equipment.

questions.q: Which statement about people with medical conditions or limitations is correct according to the manual?
options: They can drive only if they pass a new road test every single year
They may drive only if a licensed adult rides with them on every trip
They can never be licensed again once a condition appears after first licensing
They may still drive safely if the condition is stable and doctor-monitored
questions.ref: p.9 Limited Licenses Program: a person with certain conditions may still be able to drive safely if such conditions have been stabilized and are monitored by the person's physician.

questions.q: A permanent Connecticut resident with a disability wants training to drive with special adaptive equipment. Which agency does the manual say to contact?
options: The DMV Medical Review Division
The Office of the Secretary of State
The state Bureau of Rehabilitation Services
A licensed Connecticut commercial driving school
questions.ref: p.9 Disabled Driver Training Services: residents interested in the program should contact the state Bureau of Rehabilitation Services.

questions.q: The DMV's teen safe driving message in the manual says "You're NOT just along for the ride." Who does it say has a responsibility for safety?
options: Only the driver who holds the license
Only the driving school instructors
Only parents who set household rules
Everyone, including teen passengers
questions.ref: p.10 Teen safe driving page ("There are two ways to go"): Safety is EVERYONE's responsibility. Teen drivers and passengers like you have a responsibility for safety, too.

questions.q: Which statement about a vehicle that is in bad shape is TRUE according to the manual?
options: It costs less to run since you skip the repairs
It is safe as long as it passed its last emissions test
It costs more to run than one that is maintained
It gives you an extra safety margin in an emergency
questions.ref: p.11 Know Your Vehicle Inside and Out: a vehicle in bad shape is unsafe and costs more to run than one that is maintained; a vehicle in good shape gives an extra safety margin.

questions.q: While stopping at a light, your brake pedal sinks all the way to the floor. What does the manual say to do?
options: Replace the bulbs in the brake lights
Have the headlights realigned
Have a mechanic check the brakes
Add air to all four tires
questions.ref: p.11 Braking System: if the brakes make a lot of noise, emit an unusual odor, or the brake pedal goes to the floor, have a mechanic check them.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT listed in the manual as a sign that your brakes should be checked by a mechanic?
options: The steering wheel is hard to turn when parked
The car pulls to one side when braking
The brakes give off an unusual odor
The brakes make a lot of noise when they are used
questions.ref: p.11 Braking System: have brakes checked if they make a lot of noise, emit an unusual odor, the pedal goes to the floor, or the vehicle pulls to one side when braking.

questions.q: How does the manual say you should check that your turn signals, brake lights, taillights, and headlights are working?
options: Only at night on the road
From the dashboard lights
From outside the vehicle
Only at an emissions station
questions.ref: p.11 Lights: make sure turn signals, brake lights, taillights, and headlights are operating properly; these should be checked from the outside of the vehicle.

questions.q: Your windshield wiper blades leave streaks and are not clearing water well. What does the manual say to do?
options: Run them at full speed
Replace the blades
Only use them in snow
Use the defroster instead
questions.ref: p.11 Windshield, Wipers, Windows: if the blades are not clearing water well, replace them.

questions.q: Why does the manual say to keep the inside of your windshield and windows clean?
options: Smudges on the inside can make the windshield glass crack in cold weather
Bright sun or headlights on a dirty windshield make it hard to see
A dirty windshield will make the car fail the emissions inspection
Dirt on the inside of the glass can make the defroster stop working
questions.ref: p.11 Windshield, Wipers, Windows: make sure the inside of the windshield and windows are clean; bright sun or headlights on a dirty windshield make it hard to see.

questions.q: Your windshield has a crack from a stone chip. What does the manual recommend?
options: Replace it only if the crack grows larger
Leave it alone unless it blocks your view
Cover the crack with clear tape to seal it
Have the damaged windshield replaced
questions.ref: p.11 Windshield, Wipers, Windows: damaged glass can break very easily in a minor collision or when something hits the windshield; have a damaged windshield replaced.

questions.q: Which statement about windshield wipers is TRUE according to the manual?
options: Wipers are needed for rain only, so they don't matter in snow
Some vehicles also have wipers for the rear window and headlights
Wiper blades only need to be replaced when the windshield is replaced
The window washer bottle should be kept only half full in winter
questions.ref: p.11 Windshield, Wipers, Windows: wipers keep rain and snow off the windshield; some vehicles have wipers for rear windows and headlights; keep your window washer bottle full.

questions.q: You are driving on a wet road with worn, bald tires. According to the manual, what effect do the tires have?
options: No effect unless the tire pressure is also low
Better grip because more rubber touches the road
Longer stopping distance and harder turning
Lower risk of hydroplaning on standing water
questions.ref: p.11 Tires: worn or bald tires can increase your stopping distance and make turning more difficult when the road is wet; worn tires increase hydroplaning.

questions.q: Which statement about worn tires is FALSE according to the manual?
options: They lower the chance of a flat tire
They make turning harder on wet roads
They can increase your stopping distance
They increase the effect of hydroplaning
questions.ref: p.11 Tires: worn tires increase the effect of hydroplaning and increase the chance of having a flat tire; worn or bald tires increase stopping distance and make turning harder when wet.

questions.q: While driving, your car bounces and the steering wheel shakes. What does the manual say to do?
options: Speed up slightly to smooth out the ride
Use only the parking brake to slow down
Have a mechanic check it
Let some air out of all four tires
questions.ref: p.11 Tires: if the vehicle bounces, the steering wheel shakes, or the vehicle pulls to one side, have a mechanic check it.

questions.q: How often does the manual say you should check your tires for wear and damage?
options: Only when a tire warning light comes on
Once every month, or before a long trip
Every time you fill up the gas tank
Once a year, at the emissions test
questions.ref: p.11 Tires: once every month, or before you embark upon a long road trip, check your tires for wear and damage problems.

questions.q: You are about to do the penny test on your tire. Where on the tire should you place the penny?
options: At a point where the tread appears to be highest
On the tire sidewall next to the psi rating
At a point where the tread appears to be lowest
Between the tire and the edge of the wheel rim
questions.ref: p.11 Tires (penny test): select a point on your tire where the tread appears to be lowest and place Lincoln's head into one of the grooves.

questions.q: You turn off a paved road onto a long dirt road. According to the manual, how does this change your driving?
options: You have less traction, so stopping takes longer and skids are easier when turning
Traction improves because loose dirt helps the tires grip, so you can keep your speed
Traction is lower, but only when braking; turning on dirt is no harder than on asphalt
Traction is the same as asphalt as long as your tires have the correct air pressure
questions.ref: p.25 Tire Conditions: there is less traction on gravel or dirt than on concrete or asphalt; you must slow down, stopping takes much longer and it is easier to skid when turning.

questions.q: Bald or badly worn tires are on your car and it starts to rain. Compared with good tires, when will they begin to lose traction on the wet road?
options: At much lower speeds than about 35 mph
Only above 55 mph, when hydroplaning begins for all tires
Only in heavy rain; in light rain worn tires grip like new ones
At about 35 mph, the same speed as tires in good condition
questions.ref: p.25 Water on the Roadway: most tires have good traction up to about 35 mph on wet roads; bald or badly worn tires lose traction at much lower speeds.

questions.q: While driving in the rain, it feels like your tires have lost traction. You must make a turn to avoid a hazard. According to the manual, how should you turn?
options: Sharply, while pressing the brake pedal firmly
Quickly, so you spend less time on the water
After speeding up slightly so the tires bite into the road
Slowly, or you will cause the vehicle to skid
questions.ref: p.25 Water on the Roadway: keep the wheel straight; only turn in an emergency, and if you must turn, do it slowly or you will cause the vehicle to skid.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT one of the reasons the manual gives for the increase in aggressive driving incidents?
options: Higher posted speed limits on interstate highways
Increased traffic congestion on roads
A general decline in courtesy and civility
Youths who drive but lack the maturity to handle tense situations
questions.ref: p.25-26 Reasons for Aggressive Driving: congestion, parents modeling aggression, decline in courtesy, immature youth drivers, outside conflicts, sense of territory, false sense of safety; speed limits are not listed.

questions.q: A driver believes he owns the space around his car and wants to strike back whenever another vehicle 'invades' it. Which cause of aggressive driving does the manual say this is?
options: A false sense of immunity in safer vehicles
Conflicts from family or job issues
Increased traffic congestion
A sense of territory
questions.ref: p.26 Reasons for Aggressive Driving: a sense of 'territory' leads people to presume they own the space around their vehicles and to strike back when it is invaded.

questions.q: Another driver cuts you off aggressively and keeps driving dangerously. According to the manual, what is the best way to handle it?
options: Follow closely so you can read the license plate to report it
Flash your high beams so the driver knows it was noticed
Pull alongside at the next light and explain the danger calmly
Leave punishment to police; report it when you arrive
questions.ref: p.26 How to Avoid Conflict on the Road: leave punishment to the police; call the police to report aggressive driving when you arrive at your destination.

questions.q: A driver in the next lane keeps speeding up whenever you do, as if trying to race you. What does the manual advise?
options: Don't compete; let the driver who is racing pass you
Hold your speed so the other driver cannot get ahead
Speed up briefly to get clear of the other driver
Sound your horn to warn the driver to stop racing
questions.ref: p.26 How to Avoid Conflict on the Road: don't compete on the road; driving is not a contest; let others who are racing pass you.

questions.q: According to the manual, how should you think about another driver who has just done something aggressive to you?
options: Assume it was on purpose and stay right behind to watch the driver
Assume the driver is impaired and follow until police arrive
Give the benefit of the doubt; it was likely a mistake
Assume the driver wants to race and move out of the way fast
questions.ref: p.26 How to Avoid Conflict on the Road: give an aggressive driver the benefit of the doubt; he or she likely made a mistake from fatigue or inattention, not intentionally.

questions.q: You are cruising on a multi-lane highway in the far left lane and a faster car comes up behind you. What does the manual say about lane blocking?
options: Stay in the left lane at the limit; the other driver must wait
Yield to the right and let the faster car pass
Speed up to match the flow so you can stay in the passing lane
Tap your brakes so the driver backs off before you move over
questions.ref: p.26 Behaviors That Can Cause Trouble, Lane Blocking: don't block the passing lane; stay out of the far left lane and yield to the right for any vehicle that wants to pass.

questions.q: In a non-emergency, you need to get another driver's attention. How does the manual say you should use your horn?
options: Give one long, firm blast
Tap it lightly
Hold it until the driver responds
Honk twice quickly
questions.ref: p.26 Behaviors That Can Cause Trouble, Horn: use your horn sparingly; in a non-emergency, tap your horn lightly.

questions.q: You are not planning to turn right at the next few intersections. According to the manual's list of behaviors that can cause trouble, what should you do?
options: Avoid the right-hand lane
Stay in the right-hand lane and let drivers go around you
Use the far left lane until you need to turn
Use the right lane, since it is the slowest lane
